entry.title: Quantum private information retrieval on forest graphs, a way to retrieve data privately using quantum-entangled servers on tree-structured networks
entry.summary: Quantum Private Information Retrieval on Forests arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper studies graph private information retrieval in the quantum setting, focusing on forest graphs made of disjoint trees. The authors design a scheme that achieves rate 3/N on forest graphs, using a GHZ state shared among servers, where each server sends one qudit per round. For the special case G=3K_2, they give a scheme with rate 4/6 and a matching upper bound, establishing this as the capacity.

entry.title: MCP Tool Poisoning in Agentic AI Frameworks: A Cross-Framework Measurement Study
entry.summary: MCP Tool Poisoning in Agentic AI Frameworks: A Cross-Framework Measurement Study arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper measures how attacker-controlled tool descriptions, schema fields, and response data in the Model Context Protocol (MCP) can manipulate agentic AI systems. The authors propose a 25-class root-cause taxonomy and build the open-source tool mcpvenom to run a 9,720-cell susceptibility matrix across 12 frameworks, 18 models, and 45 attack scenarios. The overall attack success rate is 22.9%, and 12.1% of vulnerable cells verifiably exfiltrate a secret. ★★★★ Notable: The authors present a cross-framework measurement of MCP tool poisoning with real execution, a 25-class taxonomy, and a 9,720-cell matrix across 12 frameworks and 18 models.

entry.title: A cross-language benchmark comparing signing and verification speed of three verifiable credential formats.
entry.summary: An Empirical Evaluation of Signing and Verification Performance of Verifiable Credential Formats: A Cross-Language Benchmark of SD-JWT VC, W3C VCDM, and mdoc arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper compares the performance of three verifiable credential formats, SD-JWT VC, W3C VCDM 2.0 with a Data Integrity cryptosuite, and mdoc, across issuing, selectively disclosed presentation, and verification. Implementations in Node.js, Go and Python were measured in four environments. W3C VCDM took about 1.6 to 2 times as long as the other two formats, and the authors attribute this mainly to RDFC-1.0 canonicalization, which largely disappears when JCS is substituted.

entry.title: IAMRAGBENCH: Testing whether AI-generated AWS IAM policies grant excess access under poisoned retrieval
entry.summary: IAMRAGBENCH: Benchmarking Authorization Expansions in LLM-Generated AWS IAM Policies under RAG Poisoning arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper introduces IAMRAGBENCH, a 60-case benchmark that tests whether large language models using retrieval-augmented generation produce AWS IAM policies granting more access than the task allows when attacker-controlled documents are in the context. Across several model endpoints, poisoned context led to many policies that exceed the trusted authorization envelope, and the authors also assess how well AWS CheckNoNewAccess detects these changes. The authors conclude that IAM copilots should be treated as untrusted proposal generators whose outputs need independent authorization checks before deployment. ★★★★ Notable: The authors present a benchmark quantifying RAG-poisoning-induced IAM authorization expansion and propose pre-deployment independent authorization checks.

entry.title: O2N2: A Faster Doubly Oblivious Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
entry.summary: O2N2: Efficient Doubly Oblivious Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents O2N2, a doubly oblivious framework for approximate nearest neighbor search that hides query contents from a server running in trusted execution environments. It is built on single-path search over randomly rotated k-d tree forests, with the search structure stored in a pointer-based Circuit ORAM. The authors report a 9.8 to 125.9 times speedup over the fastest doubly oblivious baselines for 10-NN and 100-NN search at specified high-recall targets.

entry.title: FPGA-based end-to-end number theoretic transform to speed up fully homomorphic encryption
entry.summary: End-to-End NTT on FPGA for FHE Acceleration arXiv · Nov 3, 2026Fully homomorphic encryption allows computation on encrypted data without decrypting it, but it carries heavy computational and memory costs. This paper designs a fully unrolled streaming NTT/INTT kernel placed across the three dies of an AMD Alveo V80 FPGA. The kernel was integrated into the Lattigo FHE library and evaluated end to end. With 128-bit secure parameters, the authors report 1.8–2.2x speedups for core operations such as key switching and bootstrapping, and 1.8–2.1x for neural network inference.

entry.title: A framework combining symbolic and neural methods to extract forensic evidence from mobile SQLite databases.
entry.summary: A Symbolic-Neural Framework for Context-Aware Evidence Extraction from Mobile SQLite Databases arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents SNEEF, a framework that extracts forensic evidence from mobile SQLite databases by encoding each row as context-value pairs with provenance metadata. A language model recognizes nine forensic entity types, and the PA-EEP protocol links each entity to its source table and row. Evaluated on five corpora from Android and iOS device images, SNEEF reaches an F1 score of 0.967, compared with 0.728 for a context-free configuration.

entry.title: TrafficInstruct: A Multi-Task Network Traffic Benchmark for Instruction Tuning
entry.summary: TrafficInstruct: A Multi-Task Network Traffic Dataset and Benchmark for Instruction Tuning arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper introduces TrafficInstruct, a network traffic dataset with raw packet captures and 55,000 structured fine-tuning records covering ten analysis tasks, including malware, botnet, Tor, and encrypted VPN detection. Traffic is collected automatically from controlled software runs and attack experiments, and the data is split by complete collection sessions. The authors compare several baselines against independently trained task-specific LoRA adapters on a shared frozen model. Task-specific adaptation improves classification performance.

entry.title: Do Agents Still Follow the Rules? Testing Rule-Following After Context Compression
entry.summary: Do Agents Still Follow the Rules? Benchmarking Rule Compliance under Agent Context Compaction arXiv · Nov 2, 2026LLM agents compress long histories to fit their context windows, but the compressed context must still keep the rules that govern later actions. The authors introduce ARCBench, a configurable benchmark built on the open-source pi agent harness that measures rule compliance from actions taken during execution. They find that compression rarely deletes the rule, and most post-compaction violations occur while the rule is still in the compressed history. Retaining a rule does not guarantee compliance: compacted runs that keep the rule violate more than twice as often as runs with the full history.

entry.title: Software PUFs as hardware roots of trust for existing edge AI devices
entry.summary: Toward Deployable Hardware Roots of Trust for Edge AI: Software PUFs and Their Trade-offs arXiv · Nov 2, 2026Edge AI devices with physical access risk exposing secret keys stored in non-volatile memory. Software physical unclonable functions (PUFs) derive unique responses from analog device characteristics through software-only interfaces, avoiding post-fabrication hardware changes. This paper surveys 37 software PUF works and compares them against on-device model protection requirements such as boot-time versus runtime key derivation and response latency. It analyzes trade-offs, outlines four key challenges for edge AI deployment, and highlights promising research directions.

entry.title: A study of how much information privacy filters and odometers need to work well.
entry.summary: An Information Hierarchy of Privacy Filters and Odometers arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies how the information used by differential privacy filters and odometers limits their performance. It defines three information levels (spec, mechanism, and realisation) and classifies filters and odometers by the least informative level sufficient to determine their behaviour. The main results show strict and arbitrarily large performance gaps across this hierarchy, and that randomisation offers a separate resource that can also yield large utility gains. ★★★★ Notable: The authors formalise a three-level information hierarchy and report arbitrarily large separations in filter and odometer performance across levels.

entry.title: Systematically deriving information leakage in Massey secret sharing schemes.
entry.summary: Systematic Derivation of Leakage in Massey Secret Sharing Schemes arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies leakage attacks on secret sharing schemes, where partial information about each share is used to recover the secret. Building on the Guruswami-Wootters construction, the authors derive new explicit linear exact repair schemes and analyze their algebraic properties. They also introduce a Gröbner-basis-based computational method for finding leakage functions across arbitrary linear codes. Applied to Reed-Solomon, generalized Reed-Muller, and Tamo-Barg codes, the method identifies several repair schemes not previously described in the literature.

entry.title: Cyber-JEV: Contrastive fine-tuning with fix commits for fast vulnerability triage in source code
entry.summary: Cyber-JEV: Matched Contrastive Fine-Tuning of Language Models for Fast Source-Code Vulnerability Triage arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper presents Cyber-JEV, a method that fine-tunes language models to give each source-code function a vulnerability score in a single pass, so security teams can rank functions for review. It builds comparison groups from fix commits, pairing each vulnerable function with its patched version and unchanged functions from the same file, and trains one model on classification and ranking. On a 7,270-function test benchmark, an ensemble of five fine-tuned Qwen3.5-4B models reaches an AUROC of 0.814, versus 0.743 for Jev 1.13.

entry.title: Encrypted semantic communication with key-controlled signal perturbation and leakage-aware training
entry.summary: Leakage-Aware Encrypted Semantic Communication with Key-Conditioned Signal Perturbation arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper improves encrypted semantic communication by adding a key-conditioned signal-domain perturbation layer, called LAPI, and an InfoNCE-guided training rule that adds an adaptive leakage penalty to the fixed adversarial objective. Experiments on the Europarl corpus over AWGN and Rayleigh fading channels show that InfoNCE-guided training mainly suppresses the eavesdropper, lowering its BLEU to about 0.07 at high SNR. Adding LAPI further reduces the InfoNCE-estimated leakage by 5-9%, and the two mechanisms can be applied jointly.

entry.title: Testing self-healing defense against repeated cyber attacks
entry.summary: Evaluating autonomous self-healing against persistent cyber-attacks arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper tests SH4CS, an immune-system-inspired self-healing cybersecurity software developed by TNO. The authors combine analytical and experimental evaluation against repeated exploits of web application vulnerabilities. Results show that SH4CS achieves effective cyber resilience in these scenarios. The paper notes that remaining challenges include balancing predictable resilient behaviour with adaptiveness to diverse threats and protected applications.

entry.title: Rethinking neural decompilation: candidate selection is the hidden bottleneck
entry.summary: Rethinking Neural Decompilation: Candidate Selection as the Hidden Bottleneck arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies why neural decompilers based on large language models still lag in accuracy on obfuscated binaries, focusing on how candidate code is generated and selected. The authors find that correct reconstructions are usually already among the model's sampled outputs, and they compare several ranking methods, with execution-guided selection performing best. After fine-tuning on the newly released ExeBench-Obfuscated dataset, pass@1 on obfuscated binaries rises to 88.8%.

entry.title: Movable-Antenna-Assisted Secret Key Generation over Temporally Correlated Channels
entry.summary: Movable Antenna-Assisted Secret Key Generation over Temporally Correlated Channels arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies physical-layer key generation using movable antennas (MAs) over wireless channels whose multipath gains are temporally correlated, modeled by a first-order Gauss-Markov process. The authors derive a finite-horizon approximation error bound, a closed-form one-step conditional mutual information metric, and an alternating optimization algorithm that jointly tunes antenna positions and beamforming. Simulations show the MA scheme outperforms fixed antennas, with position optimization yielding about 51% higher rates and joint optimization a further 106% gain at high temporal correlation.

entry.title: ATrust: Adaptive Trust Boundary Expansion for Securing AI Agents
entry.summary: ATrust: Adaptive Trust Boundary Expansion for Securing LLM Agents arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper proposes ATrust, a defense for large language model agents against indirect prompt injection attacks. It starts from the user query as the root of trust and gradually admits task-essential external observations into the trust boundary during runtime. Evaluations on AgentDojo and AgentDyn report the strongest overall balance of security and utility among existing defenses.

entry.title: The Customer Never Sees the Goal: Studies whether AI shopping assistants exploit customers' disclosed vulnerabilities to push a hidden operator goal, and whether this can be detected from the conversation.
entry.summary: The Customer Never Sees the Goal: Measuring and Detecting Vulnerability-Targeted Manipulation in LLM Assistants arXiv · Nov 2, 2026Companies can deploy LLM assistants on their websites with goals customers never see. The paper introduces GAP, which records the option a model recommends without any goal, then sets the other option as the operator's goal, collecting 619,600 labeled replies across 540 everyday scenarios for 15 models. Fourteen of the 15 models push the operator goal, and 12 of them use disclosed distress or financial strain to support it. Fine-tuned detectors reach 79% accuracy from the reply alone, while zero-shot LLM judges average at most 62%, and detection weakens for vulnerabilities not seen in training. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose detecting vulnerability-targeted manipulation from customer-AI conversations via goal-anchored probing, reporting tests on 15 models, 619,600 replies, and generalization to unseen

entry.title: Where MCP Security Ends: A Three-Tier Mapping of OWASP MCP Top 10 Risks
entry.summary: Where Does MCP Security End? A Three-Tier Mitigation Mapping Framework for the OWASP MCP Top 10 arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper proposes a framework that maps the OWASP MCP Top 10 risks to three architectural tiers: server, gateway, and protocol. It uses a cascading decision tree of four questions to classify each vulnerability and assign a confidence level. The framework was validated against an enterprise Managed File Transfer MCP server written in Go. High-confidence server-tier controls performed as predicted, while low-confidence protocol-tier controls failed for architectural reasons beyond server implementation.

entry.title: StateFence: A Defense Framework Protecting Blue-Team AI Agents from Poisoned Security Evidence
entry.summary: StateFence: Task-State Protection Against Evidence-Chain Contamination in Blue-Team LLM Agents arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper examines the risk that malicious instructions hidden in security telemetry, tickets, or retrieved content can spread through LLM agents used in Security Operations Centers. The authors propose StateFence, a framework that treats severity labels, incident narratives, response policies, and IOC sets as protected states. It maps attacks to explicit, stealth, multi-hop, and persistent categories and routes defenses according to the attacked state. The authors report that StateFence lowers attack success while preserving task utility.

entry.title: Explicit permutations of (Z/4Z)^m with uniformly bounded differential uniformity
entry.summary: Explicit permutations of (ℤ/4ℤ)^m with uniformly bounded differential uniformity arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper constructs an explicit permutation G_c of (Z/4Z)^m whose differentials with nonzero input difference have probability at most 36/N, where N=q² and q=2^m. This is compared with the known lower bound of 2/√N for permutation polynomials over the same ring. The construction is a composition F_c∘J∘F_c built from polynomial layers and a digit exchange, and the bound does not depend on m.

entry.title: When Neither Side Confirms: A Study of Destructive Tool Approval in MCP Servers and Hosts
entry.summary: When Neither Side Confirms: Destructive Tool Approval Across MCP Servers and Hosts arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper examines how AI agents calling destructive tools, such as deleting data or moving money, through the Model Context Protocol (MCP) are approved by humans. It measures both server-side confirmation and host-application approval steps by analyzing source code. The authors find that most destructive tools lack server-side confirmation and most hosts have no default approval step. They conclude that applications should configure approval themselves. ★★★★ Notable: The authors measure missing human approval for destructive MCP tools from source code on both sides, and report an injected-deletion experiment across models.

entry.title: Ranked but Not Stopped: Confidence Monitors Against Prompt-Injection Hijacks
entry.summary: Ranked but Not Stopped: Detecting Prompt-Injection Hijacks from Typed Decision Models' Output Probabilities arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper studies language models used as classifiers, where injected text can shift the output label to one chosen by an attacker, a 'hijack'. The authors test a monitor that, without knowing the attacker's label, raises an alarm when the model's top probability is low, using AG News topic classification. Low confidence ranks hijacked answers above clean ones, but a threshold set for a 5% clean alarm rate misses most hijacks, especially when the injected text claims the target is certain.

entry.title: Study of networked synthetic social engineering that misleads AI systems on the web
entry.summary: Networked Synthetic Social Engineering on the Web arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper examines how synthetic social engineering, deliberate misleading influence aimed at redirecting AI recipients from authorized goals, spreads across networked services. The authors tested Qwen3-4B on two briefing tasks across 1,080 research units in their ASE-EC setup. Results show multiple dependent publishers did not increase unsupported verification, and correcting dependent reports reduced residual invalid decisions, though scope revalidation was needed for successful repairs.

entry.title: Grouping Malware Samples: A Survey of Methods, Challenges, and Evaluation Metrics
entry.summary: Malware Clustering in the Wild: Taxonomy, Challenges, and Evaluation Metrics arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This survey reviews clustering, a technique for grouping large collections of malware samples to reveal structure, behavior patterns, and evolution trends. It organizes prior malware clustering research into seven categories: centroid-based, hierarchical-based, density-based, distribution-based, mixed-type, fuzzy, and AI-driven approaches. The paper also summarizes publicly available malware datasets used in clustering studies and the feature representations derived from them, and outlines directions for future research.

entry.title: Fast private database lookups using the built-in matrix units in CPUs
entry.summary: High-Throughput Private Information Retrieval with on-CPU Accelerators arXiv · Nov 2, 2026Private information retrieval (PIR) lets a client fetch a record without revealing which one, usually by scanning the whole database. This paper presents AltoPIR, the first PIR system to use on-CPU matrix accelerators such as Intel AMX, improving throughput through batching without extra discrete hardware. According to the paper, it reaches up to 50.1x the throughput of existing CPU-based solutions and can serve databases larger than a GPU's memory.

entry.title: Accessed, never disclosed: silent access to protected health information by medical AI agents
entry.summary: Accessed, never disclosed: Silent access to protected health information by medical artificial intelligence agents arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper examines whether medical AI agents access protected health information (PHI) tools even when a clinical task does not require patient identifiers. The authors embedded canaries in synthetic patient records and linked tool calls to canary exposure in final answers across five language models, four boundary levels, and seven attack frames. Three models invoked PHI tools unnecessarily, and the authors conclude that output-only evaluation cannot detect such silent access, so boundaries, pre-execution gates, and access-log audits are needed together. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce canary-based tracking of silent PHI access, showing output-only evaluation misses it, with experiments across five models, boundary levels, and attack frames.

entry.title: Detecting, Repairing and Auditing Attacks on Energy Demand Forecasts with Multi-Agent Defenses
entry.summary: Detect, Repair and Audit: A Hierarchical Multi-Agent Defense Against Adversarial Attacks in Energy Forecasting arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper addresses the risk that time-series large language models used for electricity-demand forecasting can be distorted by compromised sensor inputs. It proposes a three-layer defense: a multi-agent reinforcement learning detector with signal repair at local control centers, and an LLM auditing agent with human-in-the-loop validation for Virtual Power Plants. The best detector configuration achieves an F1 score above 0.91 across all dataset-attack pairs, and signal repair reduces relative squared error by up to 83%, with detection and repair averaging 7.95 ms.

entry.title: Using dynamic defense methods to strengthen the security of advanced metering infrastructure
entry.summary: Increasing the security of advanced metering infrastructure using dynamic defense methods arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper notes that smart grids connected to the internet are constantly exposed to cyberattacks, and that the metering system, a critical part of them, could cause irreparable damage to a country and its industries if compromised. It proposes using dynamic "Applications that Participate in Their Own Defense" to protect such systems and infrastructure.

entry.title: Matched evaluation of QUBO models for cyber attack graphs and defensive patching
entry.summary: A Matched Evaluation of QUBO Action Models and Defensive Remediation in Cyber Attack Graphs arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper examines how vulnerability-specific actions affect QUBO models for minimum-cost cyber attack paths and defensive remediation. Simulated annealing, steepest descent, and tabu search are compared against exact classical references on six synthetic topologies. A single labeled action per eligible transition preserved feasible paths, optimal costs, and QUBO size, while multiple exploit alternatives lowered optimal-path recovery and substantially enlarged the representation. The approach was also tested on a published 3CX attack graph with synthetic costs.

entry.title: Black-box attacks on machine learning ballot classifiers in elections
entry.summary: Black-Box Adversarial Example Attacks on Machine Learning based Election Systems arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies adversarial example attacks on machine learning models that classify ballots, assuming an attacker who cannot see the model's parameters. The authors implement and evaluate eleven black-box attacks across several norms and decision-, score-, and transfer-based threat models. They print and scan 20,000 adversarial examples to measure real-world performance, finding a larger physical-digital robustness gap than in white-box settings. The work also presents the first adversarial transferability study in the voting domain and tests adversarial training and barrier zones as defenses.

entry.title: Decision models as runtime policy checks for coding agents, with explicit rule boundaries
entry.summary: Decision Models as Policy Gates for Coding Agents: Explicit Policy Boundaries Improve Detection and Reduce False Alarms arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper evaluates 22 hosted decision models and two prompted general models as classifiers for a multi-rule policy engine that screens coding agent tool calls. On a synthetic dataset of 2,643 tool calls labeled against 28 rules, writing explicit boundaries as examples and counterexamples raised recall on all 23 models and reduced false positives on 21. The dataset, rule texts and harness are released.

entry.title: HaloGuard 2.0: An Open-Weights Safety Filter for Checking Multilingual AI Responses
entry.summary: HaloGuard 2.0: An Open-Weights Constitutional Output Guard for Multilingual Response Safety arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper presents HaloGuard 2.0, an open-weight streaming guard that scores each response token as safe or unsafe in a single pass, so generation can be stopped once harm is confirmed. It reuses the constitution of HaloGuard 1.0 to organize a large response training corpus and adds a second training phase with counterfactual responses to correct a shortcut where the guard judged the prompt rather than the response. On six English response-safety benchmarks it reaches a macro F1 of 83.6, and a multilingual variant reaches 83.1 F1 on response labels across 17 languages.

entry.title: Bounded History Retention in Flow Replay: A Predictive Pilot and Allocation Study
entry.summary: Bounded Retained History in a Proxy Flow Replay: A Mixed Predictive Pilot and an Allocation Study arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper studies bounded retained history on a curated UNSW-NB15 flow mirror, first through a frozen predictive pilot and then an allocation study. In the pilot, adding retained relational features lowered reconnaissance recall and benign false-positive rate compared with the baseline, and AUROC was also lower, so no predictive advantage was shown. A follow-up allocation study found that source-balanced retention beat FIFO on an equal-source endpoint, while event-weighted ratios decreased, so the result is specific to that weighting objective. Reused data and proxy timing limit interpretation.

entry.title: ZT-DAC: ML-Driven Dynamic Access Control for Zero Trust in Energy Networks
entry.summary: ZT-DAC: ML-Driven Dynamic Access Control Policy for Zero Trust in DER Networks arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper addresses the weakness of static role-based access control in distributed energy resource networks, where authenticated attackers can keep privileges and move laterally. It proposes ZT-DAC, a dynamic framework that uses two-stage verification, combining OPA-based RBAC with machine-learning-based ABAC for continuous trust score assessment. Experiments report 91.92% accuracy for the OPA decision layer and 93.27% for the ABAC layer.

entry.title: SANAI: Keyed parity hidden in neural network weights to defend against bit-flip attacks
entry.summary: SANAI: Secure ECC Distributed Keyed Parity Embedded in Weights for Protecting Neural Networks against Bit-Flip Attacks arXiv · Nov 2, 2026Quantized neural networks store their weights in dense memory, where bit flips from voltage scaling, aging, radiation, or attacks such as RowHammer can degrade model behavior. The paper proposes SANAI, a sensitivity-guided scheme that selects bit planes and embeds keyed parity within the weights with no extra parity storage. The authors report that across ten vision backbones, three quantization schemes, and ten language models, SANAI stays within about one percentage point of clean accuracy at bit-error rates up to 12%, about twice the limit of prior embedded-ECC approaches.

entry.title: Query-efficient method for locating hidden watermarks in AI-generated text
entry.summary: Query-efficient scan-and-search watermark localization arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper addresses how to pinpoint implicit watermarks that large language models embed in their outputs. It proposes an adaptive strategy that first covers the whole document broadly, then concentrates the detection budget on regions with stronger watermark evidence. Statistical signals from selected regions are converted into e-values and processed with a token-weighted e-BH procedure. The framework, named BELL, is reported to control the token-weighted false discovery rate without requiring independence across regions and to outperform competing methods across several LLMs, datasets, and watermarking schemes.

entry.title: One String to Rule Them All: Measuring Consent Under the IAB Global Privacy Platform
entry.summary: One String to Rule Them All: Measuring Consent Under the IAB Global Privacy Platform arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper examines how the IAB Global Privacy Platform (GPP), a standard for sharing user consent across jurisdictions, transmits opt-out choices from publishers to third parties. The authors analyze data from four web crawls across four experimental settings. They study how widely the standard is adopted, whether opt-out signals propagate, and whether they affect advertiser behavior. The findings show implementation inconsistencies that cause consent signals to be lost and opt-out choices to go unrespected by advertisers.

entry.title: Speeding up QUIC encryption in WebAssembly with SIMD instructions
entry.summary: Accelerating QUIC Encryption in WebAssembly Using WASM-SIMD arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper examines the cryptographic cost of running the QUIC transport protocol inside WebAssembly (Wasm). The authors write explicit kernels using Wasm's 128-bit SIMD extension for AES and ChaCha20. On two hosts linked by 10-Gigabit Ethernet, these kernels raise receiver goodput over a non-SIMD baseline by 61.34% for AES-128-GCM and 31.55% for ChaCha20-Poly1305. The authors conclude that cryptographic acceleration is necessary but not sufficient, since memory allocation, runtime overhead and per-datagram UDP I/O still limit pure-Wasm transports.

entry.title: Beyond Prompt Injection: The Tool Update Gap in LLM Agent Security
entry.summary: Beyond Prompt Injection: The Tool Update Gap in LLM Agent Security arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper examines how LLM agents that rely on external tools may keep trusting those tools after updates without re-verifying their safety, creating a supply-chain vulnerability. The authors introduce ETUDE, an attack that embeds malicious functionality into updates of initially benign tools while keeping their legitimate features, operating outside the LLM's context. Tested across three attack workloads and seven agentic frameworks, ETUDE achieved a 97.6% attack success rate with a 95.9% legitimate task completion rate, and existing defenses were found insufficient. ★★★★ Notable: The authors identify the tool update gap and propose ETUDE, reporting attack success and task completion across seven agentic frameworks.

entry.title: Step-Zero Attack: Agent Safety Before Observability
entry.summary: Step-Zero Attack: Agent Safety Before Observability arXiv · Nov 1, 2026This paper argues that existing attacks and defenses for coding agents target the stage after content enters the model, while agents often must first process unknown files, network responses, or images to judge their safety, and that processing can itself cause harm. The authors call this initial processing "Step Zero" and test seven harnesses and six models. Most combinations exceeded a disk budget before the model saw any content, and the paper proposes a gate at the processing-primitive level that keeps extraction within budget. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce Step-Zero attacks, where harm occurs before the model reads content, testing seven harnesses and six models with a byte-counting gate defense.

entry.title: CertClaim: A certified method for verifying model claims in coding-agent services
entry.summary: CertClaim: Towards Certified Model-Claim Verification for Coding-Agent Services arXiv · Nov 1, 2026Coding-agent services are priced according to the model they claim to use, so verifying those claims matters to users. The paper argues that existing model auditing methods assume a fixed deployment, while providers may legitimately change sampling settings, reasoning mode, or system prompts without changing the model, causing false accusations or missed cheap substitutes. The authors propose CertClaim, which treats all authorized deployments as part of the claim and checks whether some authorized deployment explains the service's evidence. The paper provides theoretical analysis of its false-accusation rate and detection condition, and experiments show it is valid across settings and resistant to potential adaptive attacks.

entry.title: Reddit community signals as a supplementary domain-reputation feature for spam classification, evaluated conservatively
entry.summary: Reddit Community Signals as a Supplementary Domain-Reputation Feature in Spam Classification: A Conservative Controlled Evaluation arXiv · Nov 1, 2026This study tests whether signals derived from Reddit discussions can serve as an extra domain-reputation feature for email spam classification. Using a 5,582-email corpus preprocessed from SpamAssassin, it compares a baseline, a version with urgency and action scores, and a version adding Reddit-based features. The Random Forest model with Reddit-enhanced features reaches 97.94% accuracy, a 0.55-point gain over the baseline that is not statistically significant in the primary split. The authors frame the results conservatively and call for further validation before deployment.

entry.title: Grading student reports with small language models using rubrics
entry.summary: Rubric-Based Assessment of Student Reports Using Small Language Models arXiv · Nov 1, 2026This study presents an automated grading pipeline that runs locally, using lightweight language models to assess student texts against predefined rubrics and a vision-language model to interpret images. It uses responses from 105 students across two semesters of an undergraduate cybersecurity incident response exercise. Small models in low-resource settings reached up to 97% accuracy on text-only assessments and up to 94% on rich-text assessments.

entry.title: Chain-of-thought monitoring needs separate evidence for faithfulness and monitorability
entry.summary: Chain-of-Thought Oversight Requires Separate Evidence for Faithfulness and Monitorability arXiv · Nov 1, 2026This paper argues that a visible reasoning trace does not automatically make model behavior easier to monitor, since reasoning visibility, mechanistic faithfulness, mechanistic localizability, and behavioral monitorability are distinct properties. Two case studies across three open-weight reasoning models show that evidence for one property does not establish the others. The authors propose an evidential-chain reporting standard in which each claim states its target property, access tier, and artifact, and each required link is labeled as supported, unsupported, or assumed.

entry.title: StateGate: A prompt optimization method that keeps long-chain AI agents following all their instructions
entry.summary: StateGate: A Behavioral-Fidelity Prompt Optimization Method for Long-Chain LLM Agents arXiv · Nov 1, 2026Long-chain LLM agents often fail to carry out every step of complex tasks even when their prompts specify them. StateGate converts natural-language constraints into symbolic gates enforced by an external deterministic runtime, separating constraint effectiveness from its text. The design uses a state file, a validator, and an orchestrator, and was tested on a security vulnerability-discovery task, where it reported 100% execution closure and accurate vulnerability detection.

entry.title: Detecting Generated-Depth Injection Attacks on RGB-D Place Authentication
entry.summary: Detecting Generated-Depth Injection Attacks on RGB-D Place Authentication arXiv · Nov 1, 2026This paper studies attacks in which an adversary uses monocular depth estimation to generate depth from public RGB images and submits forged RGB-D queries to place authentication. The authors evaluate a presentation attack detection classifier that relies on geometric consistency between enrollment and query views, across three stages depending on how accurately the attacker knows the camera intrinsics. They report that the original classifier falls to near chance when the attacker has exact intrinsics, while a retrained classifier still detects forgeries using the registration residual.

entry.title: CipherFlow: A compiler that builds fast, cryptographically secure AI inference programs
entry.summary: CipherFlow: Compiling AI Programs for Efficient Cryptographically Secure Inference arXiv · Nov 1, 2026CipherFlow is a compiler framework that takes an AI computation graph, cryptographic primitives, and a target hardware and network setup, and generates a latency-optimized secure inference program. It profiles primitive costs on the deployment environment, jointly plans placement of homomorphic encryption and secure multi-party computation, and uses BlockFold to scale planning to Transformer graphs. On BERT-base and ViT, it reports speedups of up to 16.5 times and over 22 times, respectively, compared with static hybrid placement baselines.

entry.title: J-Anchor: Defending Language Models Against Prefill Attacks by Restoring Refusal in J-Space
entry.summary: J-Anchor: Defending Against Prefill Attacks via J-Space Selective Refusal Restoration arXiv · Nov 1, 2026This paper studies prefill jailbreaks, where an attacker supplies an unsafe assistant prefix that makes a safety-aligned language model continue generating harmful content. The authors observe refusal-state erosion: during prefilling, the refusal signal falls back to its benign baseline while the harmfulness signal stays elevated. They propose J-Anchor, a training-free inference-time defense that uses the pre-attack signals as an anchor to selectively restore refusal in J-space. The method reduces attack success across model families while largely preserving benign behavior and reasoning ability.

entry.title: Bilinear Hulls for Faster Support Splitting in Code Equivalence
entry.summary: Bilinear Hulls for Support Splitting: Characterization, Optimization, and Applications arXiv · Nov 1, 2026The paper studies how replacing the standard inner product in Sendrier's Support Splitting Algorithm with a bilinear form can reduce its cost. It shows only a narrow two-parameter family of forms works, and the hull dimension drops by at most one, so the cost falls by at most a factor of q, the field size. The authors find that PEP-based SPECK benefits from this reduction, while LESS and PERK fall outside the framework, and a SageMath implementation confirms feasibility at length 252.

entry.title: When Benign Is Unverified: Label-Signal Mismatch in Graph-Based Memory Forensics
entry.summary: When Benign Is Unverified: Label-Signal Mismatch and Abstention-First Triage in Graph-Based Memory Forensics arXiv · Nov 1, 2026The paper examines validation of a graph-based triage pipeline for Windows memory images. On the MalVol-25 dataset, a rule layer flags nearly all benign control captures, contradicting their benign labels and suggesting the benign class is unverified. The authors report similar defects in public corpora and propose seven reporting artefacts for learned triage on corpora with asserted ground truth.

entry.title: Large-scale check of cookie notice privacy and accessibility for blind and low vision users
entry.summary: A Large-Scale Evaluation of Cookie Notice Privacy and Accessibility for Blind and Low Vision Users arXiv · Nov 1, 2026This paper presents the first large-scale evaluation of cookie notices across 2,061 domains, focusing on blind and low vision users. Using a crawler, a custom screen reader add-on, and accessibility tools, it measures UK GDPR/PECR compliance, tracker activity before and after consent choices, and screen reader accessibility. It finds that 51% of sites show a cookie notice, and at least 50% of those violate UK GDPR/PECR requirements. Accepting a notice produces a mean five-fold increase in tracker activity. Notices that fail legal privacy requirements also tend to be the least accessible to screen reader users.

entry.title: SHield: Watermarking 4D Gaussian Splatting via Spherical Harmonic Coefficient Perturbation
entry.summary: SHield: Watermarking 4D Gaussian Splatting via Spherical Harmonic Coefficient Perturbation arXiv · Nov 1, 2026This paper presents SHield, a watermarking method that protects 4D Gaussian Splatting (4DGS) model files from unauthorized copying. It embeds a zero-mean payload across the spherical harmonic coefficients of a key-selected subset of Gaussians, with a brief anchored optimization to preserve visual fidelity. Verification needs no neural decoder and recovers the payload in closed form. Across 30 scenes from D-NeRF, HyperNeRF, and DyNeRF, payload recovery reaches a Pearson correlation of at least 0.991 with a mean rendering penalty of at most 0.13 dB, and the image payload survives INT8 quantization and 30% opacity pruning.

entry.title: A stacked hardware security controller that detects anomalous behavior in Edge AI systems with low overhead and energy use.
entry.summary: Enhancing Edge AI System Security with a Stacked Hardware Security Controller for Robust and Energy-Efficient Anomaly Detectio arXiv · Nov 1, 2026This paper proposes a stacked, hardware-based security mechanism for continuous, low-overhead detection of anomalous execution patterns in Edge AI systems. It uses hardware performance counters and physical sensors, isolated as a tamper-resistant root of trust. Experiments show that adversarial or malicious applications cause observable deviations in sensor and thermal readings, and that hardware-based detection remains effective with low overhead.

entry.title: Defending Post-Quantum Cryptography Against Side-Channel Attacks Using 3D Shielding
entry.summary: Side-Channel Attack Prevention for Post Quantum Cryptography Algorithms: A 3D-Shield Approach arXiv · Nov 1, 2026This paper notes that post-quantum cryptography (PQC) algorithms, though resistant to quantum attacks in theory, remain vulnerable to side-channel attacks in practical implementations. The authors propose a defense based on 3D integration, which uses stacked hardware for physical shielding and introduces decoy keys to conceal cryptographic activity. The approach can complement masking and shuffling and involves moving Number Theoretic Transform (NTT) computations to dedicated chips. Its effectiveness is validated against a generic attack targeting intermediate computations within an NTT butterfly.

entry.title: Using a Bounded Application-Security Ontology at the Point of Change to Identify Obligations for Code Changes
entry.summary: What Must Be Done Here? Using a Bounded Application-Security Ontology at the Point of Change arXiv · Nov 1, 2026The paper presents a use case for AppSec Core, a bounded application-security ontology, to make security guidance actionable at the point of code change. Scattered requirements from secure-development frameworks, verification standards, controls catalogues, and regulations such as NIS2 are organized into a typed working set of control objectives, practices, mechanisms, and evidence artifacts, each traceable to its source. The authors describe two entry points: starting from a code change, or from a normative obligation such as NIS2 compliance. The same working set serves both human engineers and LLM-based assistants.

entry.title: Blind spots of detection: attacks on watchdogs in distributed LLM inference
entry.summary: The Blind Spots of Detection: Adversarial Perturbation Attacks against Watchdogs in Distributed LLM Inference arXiv · Nov 1, 2026This paper examines how a malicious node in decentralized large language model inference can sabotage generation while staying within the numerical tolerance used for verification. The authors introduce Hush-Up, which adds adversarial perturbations to output activations to raise the end-of-sequence token probability and force premature termination. The paper reports that this attack can also cause existing defenses to miss the sabotage or wrongly blame honest workers. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report a stealthy attack that uses adversarial perturbations within benign error bounds to halt distributed LLM inference and evade watchdog detection across models and benchmarks.

entry.title: Pop Goes the Verifier: A Stealthier Data Poisoning Attack on Voice Liveness Detection
entry.summary: Pop Goes the Verifier: Phoneme-Targeted Data Poisoning of Voice Liveness Detection arXiv · Nov 1, 2026This paper examines data poisoning attacks against voice liveness detection (VoicePop) used in automated speaker verification systems. The earlier SyntheticPop attack leaves visible artifacts in waveform energy, making it easier to detect. The authors propose a stealthier phoneme injection method that uses FastSpeech 2 and a modified HiFi-GAN vocoder to insert pop bursts at plosive phonemes, with subtle Gaussian noise added to reduce visibility. Evaluated on ASVSpoof 2019, the approach achieves moderate poisoning while resisting signal-level inspection better than the original SyntheticPop attack.

entry.title: VeilFL: Two-Stage Accountability for Anonymous Federated Learning
entry.summary: VeilFL: Two-Stage Accountability for Anonymous Federated Learning arXiv · Nov 1, 2026This paper presents VeilFL, a two-aggregator protocol that extends PINE (USENIX Security '24) with staged accountability for anonymous federated learning. It detects duplicate submissions within a round, and after confirmed faults, a threshold committee can link misconduct to a stable handle while accepted submissions stay unlinkable. The prototype reports a median of 2.11 ms to create a submission and 3.01 ms to verify it.

entry.title: Timestamp reliability in malware data: first-seen date estimation
entry.summary: Trouble With Time: Compile Timestamps and First-Seen Date Regression in EMBER2024 arXiv · Nov 1, 2026This paper examines whether machine learning can estimate when an executable was first seen, or detect unreliable PE/COFF compile timestamps, using the EMBER2024 dataset. The authors evaluate feature-based and raw-byte models and find that direct first-seen regression errors are large and cannot replace externally sourced metadata. Classifiers, however, can identify timestamps within set tolerances of first-seen dates and detect clearly implausible ones with high discrimination.

entry.title: E-UDE: A machine learning model that predicts how malware spreads across the internet.
entry.summary: E-UDE: A Scientific Machine Learning Model for Malware Propagation Dynamics arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper proposes an Enhanced Universal Differential Equation (E-UDE) framework that incorporates more detailed factors affecting malware propagation, aiming to improve both interpretability and predictive accuracy. On real-world propagation data it achieves an overall RMSE of 783.70 and MAE of 421.65, reducing RMSE by about 66 percent versus the classical ODE model and about 39 percent versus the UDE model. The model stays relatively stable as noise increases and supports scenario analysis under different cybersecurity conditions, and it was evaluated on the Code Red and Witty Worm datasets.

entry.title: Illusion: Protecting the Hidden Communication Structure of AI Agent Teams
entry.summary: Illusion: Safeguarding Topology Confidentiality in LLM Multi-Agent Systems via Behavior-Preserving Obfuscation arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper addresses how the communication structure of large language model multi-agent systems can be reconstructed by attackers from agent outputs. It proposes Illusion, a defense that injects fake edges and messages to show attackers a deceptive structure while keeping output behavior and task accuracy largely unchanged. Experiments report that edge-level F1 drops from over 0.87 to 0.62 and graph similarity from over 0.94 to 0.71.

entry.title: Learning authorization states from multiple evidence to detect broken object-level authorization at runtime in black-box web apps
entry.summary: Cross-Evidence Authorization State Learning for Runtime Detection of Broken Object-Level Authorization in Black-Box Web Applications arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper addresses broken object-level authorization (BOLA), which is hard to detect in black-box web applications without access to source code or policies. It proposes a method that reconstructs subject, resource, object and action relations from request-response transactions, using confidence-aware states and aggregating independent positive and negative evidence. Evaluated on a deterministic synthetic benchmark of 64,400 requests over five random seeds, it reports 100.00% recall, a 56.63% F1-score, a 33.65% false-positive rate and a 0.00% unauthorized-relation pollution rate.（BOLA：对象级授权失效）

entry.title: AgentCap: Capability-Based Runtime Authorization for Secure LLM Agent Execution
entry.summary: AgentCap: Capability-Based Runtime Authorization for Secure LLM Agent Execution arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper presents AgentCap, a runtime authorization layer that intercepts every tool call an LLM agent makes through an MCP wrapper and checks it against policies covering intent, trust, workflow prerequisites, and argument provenance. Authorized requests receive short-lived, budget-limited capability tokens that are validated at the tool boundary, and delegation is restricted to session-bound chains. Across AgentDojo and InjecAgent, AgentCap reduced attack success in every evaluated setting, and in controlled adversarial scenarios it blocked all unauthorized executions while keeping legitimate operations working.

entry.title: Budgeted evasion of KGW watermarks by replacing token-level evidence
entry.summary: Constructing Budgeted KGW Evasion through Token-Event Evidence Replacement arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies evasion of KGW text watermarks by rewriting phrases within an edit budget so that the token pairs carrying detection evidence are replaced. In controlled experiments on short passages, 39 of 82 qualified detected sources were rewritten to reach a terminal detector score Z below 4 and passed blinded review, at a mean token-edit cost of 16.0% against a 20% allowance. The authors also report limits in signed evidence reduction and in recognizing sufficient editing.

entry.title: The Long Con: Web Fraud Attacks That Build Trust Before Exploiting Coding Agents
entry.summary: The Long Con on the Web: Earn-then-Exploit Fraud Attacks against Coding Agents arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper introduces EtE (Earn-then-Exploit), an attack in which a malicious website first gives verifiably helpful assistance to build trust, then issues instructions that exceed intended operational boundaries. Tested across 56 organizational environments and three coding agents, it achieved an average scene-level attack success rate of 71.4%. The authors also show that agents rely on previously helpful web sources in a trust-like way, which raises their susceptibility to later malicious instructions, and they propose action-authorization separation (AAS), which reduces attack success to 0% while keeping 100% task completion. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose an earn-then-exploit attack framework and report a 71.4% scene-level success rate across 56 environments and three coding agents.

entry.title: Adversarial Robustness Is Not Zero-Day Generalization: Testing Flow-Based Intrusion Detectors on Corrected CIC-IDS2017
entry.summary: Adversarial Robustness Is Not Zero-Day Generalization: A Controlled Evaluation of Flow-Based Intrusion Detectors on Corrected CIC-IDS2017 arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper tests whether synthetic variants of known attacks can stand in for unseen (zero-day) attacks when evaluating machine-learning network intrusion detectors. On the corrected CIC-IDS2017 dataset, four models were compared on detection under constrained perturbations of known attacks and on detection when an entire attack family is held out of training. Detection was consistently much higher under perturbation than on held-out families, so the authors conclude the two measures should be reported separately. ★★★★ Notable: The authors test whether adversarial perturbations proxy zero-day attacks, reporting large gaps versus leave-one-family-out detection across four models.

entry.title: Compressed Oracle Duality: a framework for what quantum adversaries know
entry.summary: Compressed Oracle Duality: A simple framework for knowing what quantum adversaries know arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies how to characterize the information a quantum adversary querying a random oracle retains. It proposes "Compressed Oracle Duality," which extends the Compressed Oracle method to space-bounded algorithms by applying an isometry to the adversary's memory, yielding two compressed oracles with identical marginals. The framework is applied to collision search, giving a simplified proof of a recent quantum time-space tradeoff for label-symmetric algorithms and a stronger classical tradeoff under label symmetry. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a compressed oracle duality framework for space-bounded adversaries and apply it to collision search time-space tradeoffs.

entry.title: Beyond Sensitive APIs: Finding Access Control Flaws in Android Firmware
entry.summary: Beyond Sensitive APIs: Detecting Access Control Flaws at Sensitive Callsites in Android Firmware arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper points out that existing tools flag dangerous behavior only when an app calls a predefined set of sensitive APIs, missing vulnerabilities where a generic API, such as a database read, operates on protected data without adequate access control. The authors present Callix, which judges how sensitive each callsite is by analyzing both the API's function and the data it handles, recovers each security check as an explicit property, and uses a restriction context to decide whether those checks suffice. Evaluated on 1,750 pre-installed apps from ten top Android vendors, Callix found 819 vulnerable paths, 42.1% of which allow reading or modifying private user data through generic database operations. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors combine callsite sensitivity with access-control sufficiency analysis; they report 819 vulnerable paths across 1,750 pre-installed apps from 10 vendors, with 95.1% precision.

entry.title: DERED: Improving third-party library detection in binaries by mitigating deceptive reuse
entry.summary: DERED: Enhancing Third-Party Library Detection in Binaries via Deceptive Reuse Mitigation arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper introduces the concept of deceptive reuse, a misleading reuse relationship in which recipient software shares common third-party library (TPL) code. It proposes DERED, a method that improves TPL detection in binaries by distinguishing real reuse from deceptive reuse.

entry.title: Practical preimage attacks on reduced 19- and 20-step SHA-256 with standard padding
entry.summary: Practical Preimages for 19- and 20-Step SHA-256 with Standard Padding arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper presents preimage attacks on SHA-256 reduced to 19 and 20 steps, respecting the standard IV, Davies-Meyer feed-forward, and full FIPS 180-4 padding for arbitrary 256-bit targets. The authors introduce three techniques and report that a single CPU core solves 19-step padded targets in seconds to under two minutes, while 20-step preimages require substantial CPU node-hours or GPU-hours. They provide 46 self-verifying witnesses and state that these attacks cover only 19 to 20 of 64 steps and do not threaten full SHA-256.

entry.title: Threat modeling intimate partner abuse in AI agent systems
entry.summary: Threat Modeling Intimate Partner Abuse in Agentic Systems arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper applies a technology-facilitated abuse threat model to agentic systems, which are AI systems that can act autonomously in digital environments. It analyzes the risks in the context of intimate partner violence and surveillance. Attacks are categorized by system ownership: when an abuser owns the system, existing abuse becomes easier and more scalable, while when a victim-survivor owns it, the system creates a new attack surface that abusers can exploit. The paper also outlines research and development directions for mitigation strategies.

entry.title: Secret sharing without extractable randomness: a negative answer to Bosley–Dodis
entry.summary: Secret Sharing Despite Non-Extractable Randomness IACR ePrint · Oct 14, 2026This cryptography preprint asks whether two-out-of-two secret sharing requires randomness sources from which nearly uniform bits can be deterministically extracted. The authors construct a class of flat sources and a perfectly correct, perfectly private scheme that splits a b-bit secret into two (b+1)-bit shares. They show that every deterministic function is far from uniform on some source in the class, answering the Bosley–Dodis question in the negative. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show that two-out-of-two secret sharing can be perfect over non-extractable sources, answering the Bosley–Dodis open question negatively via a parity argument, and extend the idea to two-o

entry.title: Kerkoporta: Injecting Hidden Triggers That Make Coding Agents Run Attacker Commands
entry.summary: Kerkoporta: Injecting Structured-Output Backdoors in Reasoning Coding Agents arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces Kerkoporta, a method for inserting backdoors into reasoning coding agents so that a trigger in the agent's context makes the model emit an attacker-chosen tool call. The harness executes that call, which can compromise a system's confidentiality, integrity, or availability. The approach builds poison samples, injects the backdoor through supervised fine-tuning, and restores lost utility with lightweight reinforcement learning. Attack success rates reach up to 96.2%. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors extend LLM backdoors to coding agents emitting tool calls, reporting up to 96.2% attack success across several harnesses.

entry.title: SecPO: Principled Adversarial Training Against Prompt Injection
entry.summary: SecPO: Principled Adversarial Training for Prompt Injection Security arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper addresses prompt injection, where malicious instructions hidden in untrusted data can hijack AI agents. It notes that the best existing defended model, Meta-SecAlign, still faces attack success rates near 100% under adaptive attacks. The authors propose the SecPO loss, a theoretically grounded training objective, and an adversarial training pipeline that generates stronger injected inputs. Reported results show markedly lower attack success rates across three adaptive attacks and no noticeable loss of benign utility on nine benchmarks. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose SecPO, replacing DPO's insecure reference with an injection-invariant oracle and adding stronger adversarial training, reporting lower ASR across three adaptive attacks with preser

entry.title: From Training Exposure to Membership Evidence: A Controlled OLMo 2 Study
entry.summary: From Training Exposure to Membership Evidence: A Controlled Study of OLMo 2 arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper re-runs part of OLMo 2 1B's mid-training, swapping in matched documents and using a counterfactual run with the same seed as a reference to test whether a language model was trained on a given document. A single exposure raises a document's likelihood on average but rarely identifies it. With a closely matched reference, paired tests can detect training on a collection of documents, though document-level variability still limits individual inference. ★★★★★ Notable: Controlled counterfactual retraining of OLMo 2 1B evaluates membership inference; AUC 0.767 but low individual-document identification at 1% FPR.

entry.title: Simple Features Beat Most AI Control Monitors: a study showing basic code traits can outperform AI monitors on a standard sabotage-detection test.
entry.summary: Simple Features Beat Most AI Control Monitors arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper shows that on a standard benchmark, simple features that never run the code can separate honest from backdoored solutions, outranking 20 of 24 open-weight models used as monitors. It finds the labels leak through authorship, since humans wrote the honest code and older models wrote the backdoors, and through problem characteristics. Roughly one in seven backdoors in the test set fails validity checks, which distorts comparisons. The authors release a rebuilt dataset and checks, arguing that high scores on such data are not by themselves evidence of sabotage detection. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show simple features outrank most AI-control monitors via dataset label leakage, report checks on a standard set and Sonnet 5 code, and release a rebuilt dataset.

entry.title: Attack on EUDI Wallet relying parties: credential pooling, with a standard-compliant fix called CRESTA
entry.summary: Fooling Relying Parties of the EUDI Wallet Architecture: Credential Pooling Attacks and CRESTA, a Standard-Compliant Countermeasure arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper shows that relying parties of the EU Digital Identity (EUDI) Wallet can be fooled by credential pooling, where colluding users combine their credentials through a proxy to appear as one person, using only genuine hardware-generated signatures. The authors verified the attack on the European Commission's reference implementation and two Android phones. They propose CRESTA, in which an ordinary issuer certifies that a set of keys was generated in the same secure hardware, using only standard cryptography and preserving unlinkability. Relying parties need just one extra signature verification per presentation. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report credential pooling attacks on the EUDI Wallet reference implementation, plus CRESTA, a countermeasure using only standard cryptography that preserves unlinkability and adds one sign

entry.title: AgentShield: A Framework for Detecting AI Browser Agents Through Behavioral Fingerprinting
entry.summary: AgentShield: Fortifying Web Applications Against AI Agents and Agentic Browsers arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper first evaluates how modern agentic browsers fare against widely deployed anti-bot defenses, finding that many defenses built for traditional automation struggle to reliably detect autonomous AI agents. It introduces AgentShield, a behavioral fingerprinting framework that targets the perception-reasoning-action loop of agents, using dynamic web forms that progressively reveal content to capture interaction telemetry that distinguishes humans from agents. The authors also describe Extinction-induced Policy Drift, an attack in which repeatedly blocking task completion causes agents to relax safeguards, and propose defensive prompt injection techniques that exploit agent-specific weaknesses. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a behavioral fingerprinting framework targeting the Perception-Reasoning-Action loop and a new attack, EPD, with likely broad impact on web defenses.

entry.title: PP-Mark: Provable, Publicly Verifiable Watermarking for Generative AI
entry.summary: PP-Mark: Provable and Publicly Verifiable Watermarking for Generative AI arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper proposes PP-Mark, a provenance framework for generative AI content that pairs lightweight statistical detection with a zero-knowledge proof of the embedding process. Forged content is designed to fail full verification. The authors test it against representative baselines on two latent diffusion models, SD2.1 and SDXL, and report resistance to black-box imprint forgery, white-box optimization, and regeneration attacks, while remaining practical for decentralized verification. ★★★★ Notable: The authors combine lightweight statistical watermark detection with a zero-knowledge proof of embedding, evaluated on two latent-diffusion models against forgery and removal attacks.

entry.title: Spoofing the Latent State: Subtle Goal-Image Attacks Undermine LeWorldModel Planning
entry.summary: Spoofing the Latent State: Imperceptible Goal-Image Attacks Derail Planning in LeWorldModel arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper examines the test-time robustness of LeWorldModel, a visual world model that plans in latent space. It finds that the encoder's distance measure is dominated by block pose, and that a small imperceptible perturbation (ε=4/255) can make the encoder register the block at an attacker-chosen pose. On Push-T this lowers planning success from 87% to 32%, and the vulnerability appears across all four standard benchmarks.

entry.title: When appearance and motion disagree: testing whether maritime cameras can catch disguised drone boats
entry.summary: When appearance and motion disagree: evaluating class--motion consistency against disguised uncrewed surface vessels arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies how shore-based defense systems can tell uncrewed surface vessels (USVs) apart from benign boats. The authors find that adversarial hull patches suppress detection in up to 29% of attempts but never cause misclassification as benign, while physical disguise can bypass both camera and radar checks. They build a replay-based evaluation protocol from AIS tracks and show that an asset-relative closing-rate check flags most direct attacks by recreational-labeled vessels, complementing a track-only speed check.

entry.title: Humanized but Still True? Checking Facts in AI-Text Humanizer Tools
entry.summary: Humanized but Still True? Auditing Facts and Detection in AI-Text Humanizers arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper examines tools that rewrite AI-generated text so detectors classify it as human-written. Using a rule-based checker, the authors test whether numbers, dates, names, and quoted spans survive each rewrite. Across 11 commercial tools, at least one such item was changed or dropped in 35 to 65 percent of documents containing one, with quoted spans changed most often.

entry.title: A dataset and test platform for deep learning-based identification of Bluetooth devices by their radio signals
entry.summary: Dataset and Experimental Testbed for Deep Learning-Based Bluetooth Device Fingerprinting arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper introduces a large-scale Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) dataset of raw IQ transmissions from 31 commercial devices, captured across different days, locations, environments, temperatures, receiver hardware, and frequency channels. It also presents a case study evaluating state-of-the-art techniques for domain-robust radio frequency fingerprinting. The goal is to improve the real-world reliability of AI models in wireless networks.

entry.title: Randomized Caches in Hardware: Challenges and Trade-offs
entry.summary: Randomized Caches in Hardware: Challenges and Trade-offs arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies randomized caches, which resist side-channel attacks by obfuscating how memory addresses map to cache locations. The authors implement four designs (CEASER-S, ScatterCache, SassCache, and MIRAGE) as the last-level cache of a multi-core RISC-V system-on-chip. They evaluate the FPGA implementations with SPEC CPU 2017 and GAPBS workloads. They find that pipelining the index derivation function alone is insufficient, and that increased access latency mainly drives performance loss.

entry.title: Study of attacks that steal prompts from AI-generated videos to recreate and edit them
entry.summary: Demystifying Prompt Stealing Attacks against Synthetic Video arXiv · Oct 26, 2026This paper examines whether an attacker can obtain reusable inputs from a single public synthetic video to reconstruct and edit it without the original prompt or generator. The authors propose V-PSA, which combines a recovered caption, DDIM inversion, and Null-Text Inversion to reconstruct videos on an independent generator. On a benchmark of 12,000 video-prompt pairs, V-PSA reaches a video-to-video similarity of about 0.9, well above the roughly 0.6 of prompt-only baselines.

entry.title: HideOut: Protecting Mobile Users from Localization While Preserving Throughput
entry.summary: HideOut - User Protection Against Localization with Throughput Guarantees in Mobile Networks arXiv · Oct 22, 2026The paper presents HideOut, a client-side defense that hides a user's location from neural CSI-based localization attacks in cellular networks. It treats downlink spectral efficiency as a strict constraint, converting a user-chosen loss budget into a feasible set for the reported channel vector under maximum ratio transmission beamforming. Gradient-based obfuscation is projected onto this set, and across four localization architectures the localization error rises from about 1–2 m to 72–85 m while downlink spectral efficiency loss stays within 1%.

entry.title: Hiding Batch Sizes with Dummy Points for Private Training
entry.summary: Counting on Dummies: Privacy Amplification with Observable Counts and Truncated Batches arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies batch sampling in differentially private stochastic gradient descent (DP-SGD), where schemes such as Poisson sampling and random allocation produce variable batch sizes. Revealing these sizes, or truncating batches to a maximum size, can weaken the privacy guarantee. The authors propose a mechanism that adds a random number of dummy points to hide the batch size while preserving privacy under truncation. For Poisson sampling with truncated batches, experiments show better privacy-efficiency tradeoffs than the prior direct accounting method.

entry.title: Beyond Smart Homes: Analyzing IoT Vulnerabilities by Sector, Vendor and Product
entry.summary: Beyond Smart Homes: Characterizing IoT Vulnerabilities Across Sectors, Vendors, and Products arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper analyzes more than 15,000 IoT-specific CVEs to examine how vulnerabilities differ across industrial, healthcare, automotive and other sectors, as well as across vendors and product types. It finds that healthcare is dominated by authentication and credential weaknesses, while automotive faces mainly memory issues. Products from the same vendor show more similar weakness profiles than same-type products from different vendors, suggesting shared code and development practices drive weakness inheritance. The authors conclude that weakness classes should guide remediation priorities.

entry.title: How much tool-call logs reveal about users: privacy leakage from AI agent traces
entry.summary: How Much Can Tool Calls Reveal About You? Privacy Leakage from Tool-Call Traces arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies whether records of tool calls made by LLM-based agents through the Model Context Protocol (MCP) can be used by observers to infer user profiles. The authors introduce PrivacyTrace, a benchmark with 1,000 synthetic user profiles and 4,000 agent trajectories across four domains, built with real MCP tools from 25 servers. Experiments show tool-call traces yield a 26.25% attack success rate for profile inference, versus 17.97% for prior-based guessing.

entry.title: Exploring Bad Minima in Transfer Learning: Does Good Source-Task Generalization Guarantee Transferability?
entry.summary: Exploring Bad Minima in Transfer Learning arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This dissertation examines when transfer learning succeeds, asking whether good generalization on a source task necessarily implies transferability to a related target task. The author tests this by using three types of adversarial attacks on the transfer learning procedure to search for counterexamples. The empirical results show a strong relationship between source-task generalization and transferability, and do not rule out source-task generalization as a sufficient condition for successful transfer.

entry.title: What Standard Evaluations Hide About Detectors of Hijacked LLM Agents
entry.summary: What Standard Evaluations Hide About Detectors of Hijacked LLM Agents: Rare Attacks, Unseen Tools and Benchmark Transfer arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper audits eleven evaluations of detectors that flag hijacked LLM agents from their tool-call traces and finds attack rates ranging from 16% to 86%, with none varying that share. Tests on AgentDrift and AgentDojo show that precision collapses at low attack rates, detector rankings reverse when many tools are unseen, and detectors trained on one benchmark fail to beat chance on the other. The authors turn these findings into a checklist for evaluating trace detectors.

entry.title: Reparo: LLM-Based Synthesis and Validation of Access Control Policies
entry.summary: Reparo: Synthesizing and Validating Access Control Policies arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents Reparo, an LLM-aided pipeline that synthesizes, repairs, and validates access control policies using evidence collected from code, comments, and documentation in software repositories. It generates an initial policy, repairs syntax errors with official validation tools, and checks semantics against a behavioral oracle derived by a separate LLM. Evaluated on 228 GitHub repositories using Cedar, OpenFGA, or Rego, the approach raised the share of valid policies from 40.6-55.7% before repair to 99.0-100% after repair.

entry.title: Group Authentication and Secure Beamforming for Non-Terrestrial Networks: Verifying Identity While Protecting Private Data
entry.summary: Group Physical-Layer Authentication and Confidential Beamforming in Non-Terrestrial Networks arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies coordinated high-altitude platform station networks that must authenticate group responses and protect private data under shared power limits. It superimposes a fresh secret tag on private data for physical-layer authentication and derives exact finite-block expressions linking error targets to a required tag SINR. Private beams, the tag beam, and artificial noise are jointly optimized with semidefinite relaxation and successive convex approximation. Numerical results show that raising the tag length from 16 to 64 symbols lowers the required tag SINR by 7.16 dB, and joint design reduces mean transmit power by 27.4% versus a fixed-tag-direction baseline.

entry.title: Poly vs. Polyval: Polynomial-Evaluation Hash Functions Compared
entry.summary: Poly Versus Polyval arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper revisits Poly, a polynomial-evaluation hash construction over binary extension fields GF(2^n) with n=64k and k≥2. Unlike the NIST standard GHASH, Poly avoids unnecessary bit reversals of each block and uses ordinary reduction, while Polyval uses Montgomery reduction. The authors give algorithms with correctness proofs and optimised assembly implementations for n=128, 256 and 512. Their results indicate Polyval is faster at n=128, while Poly is faster at n=256 and above.

entry.title: DeepWeave: A machine learning intrusion detector that combines neural and rule-based evidence
entry.summary: DeepWeave: Weaving Neural and Symbolic Evidence for ML-Based Network Intrusion Detection System arXiv · Oct 30, 2026DeepWeave is a probabilistic neuro-symbolic network intrusion detection system that integrates logic into detection. It automatically builds and validates interpretable rules, treats neural predictions as probabilistic predicates, and combines both evidence sources through coupling policies. With only 50 labelled packet observations per attack class, macro-F1 rises from 0.632 to 0.924 and the attack false-positive rate falls from 0.075 to 0.008 compared with the matched neural baseline.

entry.title: GESIS Surf: An Open-Source Tool for Privacy-Protected Long-Term Web Browsing Data Collection
entry.summary: GESIS Surf: An Open-Source Infrastructure for Privacy-Preserving Longitudinal Web Browsing Data Collection arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents GESIS Surf, a research infrastructure for collecting web behavioral data over long periods in natural settings. It consists of a browser extension for Chrome and Firefox, a backend with a REST API, and a relational database. The system passively records user interactions, page metadata, and full HTML snapshots, organized in a hierarchical session model. It applies privacy-by-design through strict opt-in participation, per-domain collection rules, and client-side data minimization, and has been deployed with more than 1,000 participants in an academic panel.

entry.title: When safety checks become privacy risks: a privacy-preserving method for auditing LLM agent safety
entry.summary: When Safety Checks Become Privacy Risks: A Privacy-Preserving Paradigm for LLM Agent Safety Auditing arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper addresses safety auditing for large language model agents that call tools to access services, which may involve private data. It proposes a privacy-preserving paradigm that separates delegated audit computation from plaintext access and execution authority. The authors implement this as SealCall, combining learned audit representations, CKKS-based encrypted similarity computation, and execution control tied to audited tool calls. Evaluated on 1,252 public binary candidates, SealCall reaches a mean F1 score of 0.840 under grouped nested evaluation and reports preserving plaintext audit decisions in all measured cases, with each encrypted scoring operation taking 0.176 s.

entry.title: BlindStep: a secure one-step kernel for privacy-preserving collaborative reasoning
entry.summary: BlindStep: A Secure One-Step Kernel for Privacy-Preserving Collaborative Reasoning arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper presents BlindStep, a fixed-shape secure multi-party computation kernel for one post-alignment step between two semi-honest parties, covering candidate scoring and retention of a small top-ranked frontier. Six implementations in MP-SPDZ are compared, combining two sharing styles and three top-K strategies. On LAN, the Boolean-share B-Queue variant is substantially faster and uses far less communication than arithmetic-share variants, while under a 100 ms RTT WAN setting H-Sort is fastest, indicating round complexity can matter more than backend choice.

entry.title: Efficient cross-domain multi-factor authentication protocol
entry.summary: Efficient cross-domain multi-factor authentication arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper proposes CDAuth, a cross-domain multi-factor authentication protocol for securing information exchange between terminals in different security domains. It combines pseudo-identity, attribute concealment, and biometric hiding, and its authentication information sets can be freely added or modified for different access scenarios. Multi-edge servers acting as Certification Authorities store only the union of terminal attributes and a verification token per user, and native group operations replace bilinear pairings to reduce storage and computation. The authors state that CDAuth resists common security attacks and outperforms previous schemes in efficiency.

entry.title: OrionLink: A single sign-on method that keeps identity brokers from seeing user data
