entry.summary: OrionLink: Single Sign-On with Oblivious Identity Brokers arXiv · Oct 30, 2026Single Sign-On lets users access several services after one login at an Identity Provider, and many services use third-party Identity Brokers to connect to multiple providers. This paper notes that brokers can see sensitive credentials and user behavior, creating a high-value single point of failure. The authors present OrionLink, which uses unlinkable per-service pseudonyms and an anonymous key exchange that builds end-to-end encrypted channels hidden from the broker. A prototype within a brokered SSO setting shows substantial security and privacy gains with acceptable performance overhead.

entry.title: Erase the Injected Region: On-Policy Self-Distillation for Multimodal Prompt-Injection Defense
entry.summary: Erase the Injected Region: Multimodal Prompt-Injection Defense with On-Policy Self-Distillation arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper addresses multimodal indirect prompt injection, where malicious instructions are hidden in images, audio, or video that the user's task also depends on. The proposed ERASE method builds its reference by replacing the injected region with modality-appropriate blank content while keeping the rest of the media. A student model reading attacked media is trained against a frozen base model reading the erased version, using token-level feedback on its own outputs. Experiments across image, audio, and video on two model sizes report near-zero observed attack success with task accuracy close to the undefended clean-input level.

entry.title: ANGLER: An Adaptive Attack Benchmark for Web Agents with State-Based Verification
entry.summary: ANGLER: Verifier-Grounded Benchmarking with an Adaptive Attacker for Web Agents arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper introduces REEF, a benchmark of executable web environments with state-based verifiers for testing web agents against adversarial injected content. It covers 9 websites across travel, commerce, productivity, media, and communication, using 5 attack types at user and environment levels. The authors also present ANGLER, an adaptive framework that uses prior rollout outcomes to mutate attacks. Across 8 VLM-based web agents, ANGLER reaches a 20.36% attack success rate versus 15.24% for non-adaptive attacks, and lowers benign task success from 61.9% to 44.4%.

entry.title: When AI investigators cannot trust their tools: conflict-aware checking of evidence in cyber threat investigation
entry.summary: When AI Investigators Cannot Trust Their Tools: Conflict-Aware Evidence Verification for Cyber Threat Investigation arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper studies what happens when a language model combines outputs from several security detection tools that are conflicting or wrong. Unverified investigators become fragile, with accuracy falling sharply when even one of four detectors is corrupted. The authors propose Conflict-Aware Evidence Verification (CAV), which uses an equal-weight vote, a conflict gate, and an independent nearest-neighbour trust check, and report improved accuracy across corrupted conditions.

entry.title: Low-Cost AI-Assisted Reverse Engineering and Its Legal Implications
entry.summary: Cheap Reverse Engineering and What It Will Do arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper examines how generative AI makes reverse engineering faster, cheaper, and easier, enabling tasks such as identifying hardware, extracting firmware, decompiling code, and cloning apps. The authors argue this strains laws on trade secrets, copyright, anti-circumvention, computer misuse, and contracts, which have relied on reverse engineering being difficult. The paper maps these practices onto existing laws and outlines possible legal responses and their trade-offs.

entry.title: MetaVul: Automatically Discovering Agent Harnesses for Vulnerability Detection
entry.summary: MetaVul: Agentic Harness Discovery for Vulnerability Detection arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper introduces MetaVul, a self-improving framework that automatically refines the scaffolding, or harness, around LLM agents used for vulnerability detection. Starting from a structured reasoning seed, it iteratively optimizes the harness using feedback from paired vulnerable and patched functions. On a validation set of 202 pairs, optimized harnesses improve pairwise detection by up to 23.3 points, and gains carry over to a held-out set of 430 pairs. Harnesses learned with one model also transfer to another, raising held-out pairwise accuracy by 14.7 points without further optimization.

entry.title: Testing Chip Piracy Defenses Against Structural and SAT Attacks via Keystream Limits
entry.summary: Evaluating Structural and SAT Attack Resilience in Cryptographic Dynamic Logic Locking via Keystream Capping arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies dynamic logic locking, a method that protects chip designs from piracy by continuously masking signals with a cryptographic keystream. The authors move key-gates from primary outputs into internal paths and introduce a cap on keystream bit reuse to limit per-cycle exposure. On three ISCAS'85 benchmarks, internal distribution greatly enlarges the brute-force search space, and the cap causes SAT solving to time out without revealing the key.

entry.title: LanG 2.0: Energy-Efficient Agentic AI for Semi-Automated Security Operations
entry.summary: LanG 2.0: Energy-Efficient Agentic AI for Semi-Automated Security Operations at Scale arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents LanG 2.0, an agentic system that detects threats, correlates evidence and writes detection rules for security operations centers. It relies on structural safeguards, including entity-anchored correlation, human approval of rule changes and a tamper-evident ledger, rather than model accuracy. Compared with its predecessor, campaign correlation precision rose from 18.75% to 51.81% and rule acceptance from at most 60.00% to 98.33%. The authors conclude that small local models can carry most SOC detection affordably and safely under these safeguards.

entry.title: Accept Changes, Reject Attacks: Memory Management for LLM Agents
entry.summary: Accept Changes, Reject Attacks: Robust Memory Management for LLM Agents arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies how memory managers for LLM agents should update long-term memory when facts change while rejecting planted passages or injected instructions. The authors measure robustness with evidence-conditioned accuracy, which also checks that the selected records contain the needed updated evidence and no attacks. They fine-tune the manager with a simple one-shot recipe on synthesized episodes, improving scores on three backbones, though robustness remains incomplete.

entry.title: Private, low-bandwidth federated reinforcement learning for vehicle routing with quantum-safe authentication
entry.summary: Communication-Efficient Private Federated Reinforcement Learning with Post-Quantum Authentication for Vehicular Networks arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies federated reinforcement learning for cooperative vehicle routing, where vehicles share model updates instead of raw trajectory data. It proposes correlated private quantization, which uses shared randomness between paired vehicles to reduce aggregation error while keeping the same privacy guarantee and one-bit communication cost as independent quantization. The method is evaluated by coupling traffic simulation with packet-level simulation of post-quantum-authenticated vehicle-to-infrastructure communication. One-bit uploads reduce authenticated uplink size by 92.4%, and correlated quantization lowers mean travel time by 14.3% relative to independent quantization at a privacy budget of 1.

entry.title: A framework for assessing how cyberattacks on water systems could cause physical harm, tested by simulation.
entry.summary: Closing the Applied Cybersecurity Gap in Critical Infrastructure: A Cyber-to-Physical Security Assessment Framework for Water Systems arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper revisits the Applied Cybersecurity Gap framework and evaluates an experimental index (ACGI) together with a Cyber-to-Physical Propagation Rate (CPPR). It uses 2,160 synthetic trials across three water-network benchmarks, including EPANET Net3, combining cyber-attack progression rules with hydraulic simulations. The authors compare a machine-learning model against a scenario-only baseline and test how CPPR responds to physical-impact thresholds and control-blocking assumptions. The work offers a reproducible simulation workflow but does not calibrate cybersecurity control effectiveness in the field.

entry.title: Recovering Expert-Usage Patterns in Fine-Tuned Mixture-of-Experts Language Models
entry.summary: Characterizing Recoverable Expert-Utilization Signatures in Fine-Tuned Mixture-of-Experts LLMs arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies "structural memorization" in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) large language models, where a fine-tuned model retains not only its training data but also the internal expert pathways used to process it. The authors show these routing patterns can be recovered through unconditional generation using only routing and output logits, without knowledge of the fine-tuning data. They also find that traditional membership inference metrics miss these memorized structures, and propose composite metrics combining reference-model tail likelihood with complexity-aware normalization to improve detection.

entry.title: Adaptive security framework for operational technology against AI-driven attacks
entry.summary: Adaptive Dynamic Security for Operational Technology Against AI-Powered Attacks arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents ADS-OT, an adaptive dynamic security framework that models operational technology defense as a partially observable decision problem. A reinforcement-learning policy adjusts monitoring, access control, deception, and segmentation under a safety-governance layer. Compared with static baselines, the approach reduces attack-path completion and improves detection and containment.

entry.title: Elastic least privilege: letting AI agent planners manage their own temporary permissions
entry.summary: Towards Elastic Least Privilege for Agent Planning arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper proposes elastic least privilege, in which an AI agent starts with a small baseline of authority and can acquire more within an owner-defined envelope. Elevated permissions are leased and measured against a replenishing budget, with costs rising for greater power, proximity to safety invariants, and repeated requests. These costs are visible to the planner, which can prefer lower-privilege actions and release unneeded authority. The authors present how the approach could work and set out an open research agenda, leaving implementation and practical performance as open questions.

entry.title: Does Telling AI Agents Each Tool's Privilege Level Reduce Over-Privileged Choices?
entry.summary: Does Showing Agents the Privilege of Their Tools Reduce Over-Privileged Tool Selection? arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper examines whether language-model agents that choose among several tools to finish a task pick ones with more authority than needed. The authors ran 544 ToolPrivBench scenarios on eight models under five conditions, including a least-privilege instruction, privilege labels in tool descriptions, and a neutral-metadata control. Showing privilege information reduced over-privileged selection on models that exhibited it, while irrelevant metadata did not. Combined with the instruction, it raised safe completion rates on seven of the eight models.

entry.title: LiHA: A simple, lightweight hash-based method for authenticating packet source addresses
entry.summary: LiHA: Worse is Better for Lightweight Hash-based Source Authentication arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents LiHA, a source authentication mechanism that binds secret keys to source prefixes using longest prefix match and checks each packet with a single message authentication code, requiring no handshakes or per-flow state. It primarily protects against off-path attackers spoofing prefixes they do not control, while on-path replay remains possible until key rotation. LiHA was implemented as user-space libraries, eBPF programs, and an FPGA design; only the FPGA reached 100 Gbps single-thread throughput, and only when bypassing the kernel with a DPDK stack.

entry.title: Coupled or Independent? Fault Coupling in Agentic Medical Vision Systems
entry.summary: Coupled or Independent? Fault Coupling in Agentic Medical Vision Systems arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper examines whether tool-using vision-language agents are safer than single-shot models when the input image itself is untrusted. Using a dermatology agent, it classifies errors as single-channel or joint and tests typographic and physical image corruption. On PAD-UFES-20, typographic injection produces detectable retrieval bias while physical corruption does not, and crop-first retrieval yields 55% joint wrong agreement versus 35% for full-image retrieval. The order effect is reproduced on the independent HIBA test set.

entry.title: "Shall We Approve?" Consequence-Aware Approval for Coding Agents
entry.summary: "Shall We Approve?" Consequence-Aware Approval for Autonomous Coding Agents arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents Caper, an approval mechanism for autonomous coding agents that decides whether shell commands may run. Caper pre-executes each command in a snapshotted sandbox, gives an independent approver a bounded report of observed effects, commits allowed commands, and rolls back blocked ones with an actionable reason. On the SABER benchmark and the authors' YoloFS-Ext benchmark, Caper achieves the lowest harmful-outcome rate among six compared systems, while blocking 1.0% of the safe twin tasks of the dangerous ones in YoloFS-Ext.

entry.title: Safin-1.5: A safety-built model with verifiable formal reasoning
entry.summary: Safin-1.5: Safety-Native Architecture and Verifiable Reasoning for Recursive Safety Improvement arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents Safin-1.5, a language model trained through recursive safety improvement, in which safety is developed alongside general capabilities. Its architecture uses persistent safety states and moves hazardous knowledge into removable experts, while a discovery-evaluation-repair loop accepts updates only if safety improves without losing general ability or increasing over-refusal. An inference-time harness pairs the model with symbolic solvers to produce checkable formal proofs. The authors report that Safin-1.5 outperforms frontier models on safety and reasoning.

entry.title: CLIC: A Closed-Loop Layer for Securing LLM-Driven Control in Open RAN
entry.summary: CLIC: Closed-Loop Intent Consistency for Securing LLM-Driven Control in Open RAN arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper proposes CLIC, a closed-loop intent-consistency layer that defends LLM-driven control in Open RAN against runtime prompt injection and residual virtual prompt injection (VPI) attacks. It uses a small quantized language model to compute a consistency score, deployed as a Non-RT rApp for model-integrity certification and a Near-RT xApp for runtime enforcement. Evaluated on the OpenAI Cellular platform, CLIC reduces attack success rate from 0.92 to 0.29 and residual VPI attacks from 0.37 to 0.04, with about 27 ms of added latency.

entry.title: Blocking attacks isn't the same as safety: what attack success rate misses in RAG defenses
entry.summary: Prevented is Not Protected: What Attack Success Rate Hides about RAG arXiv · Oct 30, 2026Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems can be manipulated by knowledge poisoning, where attackers alter retrieved evidence. Existing defenses are mostly judged by attack success rate, which hides failures caused by the defenses themselves. The paper proposes Aligned RAG Evaluation, which compares clean and poisoned responses for the same query with and without defense. Experiments on HotpotQA and Natural Questions show that current defenses can block some attacks yet introduce unexpected target-positive answers, and that the evaluation criteria can change how defenses rank.

entry.title: RiskyPy: Model-calibrated prompt generation for jointly evaluating security and functionality of LLM-generated code
entry.summary: RiskyPy: Toward Model-Calibrated Prompt Generation for Joint Security and Functionality Evaluation of LLM-Generated Code arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper introduces RiskyPy, an automated pipeline that generates security-oriented code-generation datasets calibrated to model proficiency. Applied to Python, it covers 18 CWEs from the 2025 CWE Top 25 and produces 101 prompts. Experiments on Qwen3-4B and Seed-Coder-8B show that 57-72% of prompts yield functional code, while only 5-10% of generations have no Bandit findings.

entry.title: How LLM agents behave when a local file shadows a trusted module
entry.summary: Characterizing LLM Agent Behaviors in Module Shadowing Environments arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper presents an evaluation framework that codes agent observation, reasoning, execution, and response behaviors and aligns them with independent environmental records to reconstruct execution histories and verify final reports. It applies the framework to module shadowing, where a local file is loaded in place of a trusted module during import, enabling untrusted code execution without adversarial prompts. Across 90 trials with 15 models, the payload executed in 51% of direct shadowing trials and 87% of indirect shadowing trials.

entry.title: PrivacyFlow: Protecting Privacy in AI Agents via Information Flow Analysis and Risk Management
entry.summary: PrivacyFlow: Privacy in AI Agents through Information Flow Analysis and Consequence-Aware Risk Management arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper addresses AI agents that carry out multi-step tasks on personal data and can leak sensitive information out of context. It introduces agentic PrivacyBench, a benchmark of 5,873 tasks in 986 sequences, and PrivacyFlow, a defense that plans data sharing before execution by tracing data flows, simulating inference by recipients, and weighing risk against task utility. Across six models, PrivacyFlow reduces step-level privacy failures and raises the share of task sequences completed without a detected violation by 22 to 55 percentage points.

entry.title: Whether attacks on quantum intrusion detectors carry from simulation to real quantum hardware
entry.summary: FGSM Attack Transferability from Simulation to Quantum Hardware in Network Intrusion Detection arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper trains a hybrid variational quantum classifier on the Friday DDoS subset of CICIDS2017 and tests it with label flipping during training and FGSM evasion attacks at prediction time. Experiments run in simulation and on IBM's Fez superconducting processor. Models with similar accuracy differ markedly in vulnerability, and attacks built in simulation also work on hardware, while device noise is not treated as a defense.

entry.title: Stop Calling Them Provers: ProVerif and Tamarin Should Be Called Symbolic Protocol Analyzers
entry.summary: Stop Calling Them Provers: The Case for Calling ProVerif and Tamarin Symbolic Protocol Analyzers IACR ePrint · Oct 29, 2026This paper examines what a claim that a cryptographic protocol is proved secure depends on, including the underlying theory, the analysis software, the protocol model and the security property checked, using ProVerif and Tamarin as cases. The author audits their published soundness arguments and finds false statements, missing proofs and gaps between the procedures justified on paper and those the tools actually run, and reproduces earlier bugs that cause Tamarin to accept false claims about submitted models. The paper argues that calling these tools "provers" is misleading and that they should be called symbolic protocol analyzers, with results reported alongside the models, assumptions and evidence supporting them.

entry.title: Faster block basis reduction for linear codes
entry.summary: Quasi-polynomial time algorithms for block basis reduction of linear codes IACR ePrint · Oct 29, 2026This paper improves the block code basis reduction algorithm (BKZ) for linear codes, whose original complexity bounds required exponentially many calls to a minimum weight codeword oracle. The authors propose truncated, restricted, and DeepBKZ-based variants that run in polynomial or quasi-polynomial numbers of oracle calls. They provide an implementation for block sizes up to 24 and more, along with concrete complexity estimates and approximation-factor analysis for the low-weight codeword problem on random linear codes.

entry.title: Nenya: Efficient zkSNARKs for Integer Rings Z/2kZ Using Reverse Multiplication-Friendly Embeddings
entry.summary: Nenya: Efficient zkSNARKs for Integer Rings Z/2kZ via Reverse Multiplication-Friendly Embeddings IACR ePrint · Oct 29, 2026This paper introduces Nenya, a practical zkSNARK scheme that natively supports arithmetic over the integer ring Z/2kZ, which matches fixed-width integer types in programming languages. It reduces R1CS constraints over this ring to constraints over Galois rings using reverse multiplication-friendly embeddings, and uses a polynomial commitment scheme based on error-correcting codes. Experiments report a 4.8-second prover time for a 2^25 constraint system over 32-bit integers, about four orders of magnitude faster than the prior integer-ring SNARK. ★★★★ Notable: The authors present a SNARK supporting native Z/2^kZ arithmetic via RMFEs and code-based commitments, reporting 4.8 s prover time for 32-bit data-parallel circuits.

entry.title: Beyond the Scope of This Paper: Practical Attacks Exploiting Flash Timing on Microcontrollers
entry.summary: Beyond the Scope of This Paper: Practical Flash-Accelerator and Cache-Collision Timing Attacks on Microcontrollers IACR ePrint · Oct 29, 2026This paper shows that the flash memory architecture of almost all microcontrollers creates the same timing collisions exploited by classic cache-collision attacks, a leakage channel previously underestimated. The authors recover AES keys from as few as 750 traces across six cryptographic libraries, eight architectures and over twenty devices. They also demonstrate practical attacks on SPI bootloaders, Ethernet applications, CTAP2 over USB and 802.15.4 wireless protocols, and introduce the open-source tool FlashWhisperer. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend cache-collision attacks to microcontroller flash accelerators, reporting AES key recovery with about 750 traces across many devices and libraries.

entry.title: Smoothness of shortest isogenies between supersingular curves and their Frobenius conjugates
entry.summary: Smoothness of Shortest Isogenies to Frobenius Conjugatess IACR ePrint · Oct 29, 2026The paper studies the smoothness probability of the minimal degree δ_E of isogenies from a random supersingular elliptic curve E to its Frobenius conjugate E^(p) over the algebraic closure of a finite field. It establishes bounds for this probability. These bounds confirm that Wesolowski's p^(1/3+o(1)) attack on the supersingular endomorphism ring problem holds unconditionally. The paper also gives a uniform asymptotic formula, whose main term uses Dirichlet L-values, for the probability that a connecting isogeny of degree n exists between E and E^(p). ★★★★ Notable: The authors bound the smoothness probability of minimal Frobenius-conjugate isogeny degrees, unconditionally supporting Wesolowski's attack, and give a uniform asymptotic formula via Dirichlet L-value

entry.title: Boolean functions on 375 variables with higher nonlinearity than a known direct-sum construction
entry.summary: (Balanced) Boolean Functions on 375 Variables with Nonlinearity Exceeding the Patterson-Wiedemann Direct-Sum Bound IACR ePrint · Oct 29, 2026This paper constructs Boolean functions on 375 variables whose nonlinearity exceeds that of a direct sum of a 15-variable Patterson-Wiedemann function and a bent function. The support is built from prescribed cosets together with a subset of a multiplicative subgroup, and Gauss sum evaluation reduces the problem to a 0-1 linear feasibility problem solved via a potential criterion. The result extends to all odd n ≥ 375, and balanced versions are also obtained. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend the Patterson-Wiedemann direct-sum nonlinearity bound to 375 variables via existence proofs using Gauss sums and linear feasibility.

entry.title: High-precision noise cleaning for CKKS and its use in asynchronous threshold CKKS
entry.summary: High Precision Noise Cleaning for CKKS with Application to Asynchronous Threshold CKKS IACR ePrint · Oct 29, 2026This paper proposes a high-precision noise cleaning method for CKKS homomorphic encryption that preserves encrypted integer messages while bounding normalized output noise. It jointly chooses cleaning polynomials and evaluation parameters using an error bound covering input noise and homomorphic evaluation errors, and composes lower-degree Hermite polynomials to reduce modulus and cost. The authors apply the technique to build an asynchronous threshold CKKS scheme with strong simulation security in the random oracle model, and implement it in OpenFHE.

entry.title: Research on how well higher-order rank-based side-channel attacks work against inner product masking schemes
entry.summary: Optimality and Efficiency of Higher-Order Rank-Based Side-Channel Attacks against Inner Product Masking Schemes IACR ePrint · Oct 29, 2026This paper systematically revisits Higher-Order Spearman Coefficient Analysis (HO-SPA) for attacks on Boolean and Inner Product Masking. It proposes a variant called HO-ASPA and derives its optimal form under the Hamming weight leakage model. The authors find that, unlike HO-CPA, HO-ASPA shows no significant gap between higher-order and lower-order attacks, and it outperforms Kruskal-Wallis-based attacks. Simulated and real-world experiments are used to validate its effectiveness.

entry.title: A survey of the Hidden Subgroup Problem, from finite to infinite groups
entry.summary: From Quantum Mechanics to the Hidden Subgroup Problem: an Overview from Finite to Infinite Groups IACR ePrint · Oct 29, 2026This survey covers the Hidden Subgroup Problem, a key problem in quantum computing and computational group theory. It is linked to quantum algorithms such as Shor's factoring and discrete logarithm algorithms. The paper gathers the background needed to understand the problem, reviews recent results, and discusses open questions.

entry.title: Cryptanalysis and Enhancement of VTBSAE: Secure Password Login Protocol for Industrial IoT
entry.summary: Cryptanalysis and Enhancement of VTBSAE: Provably Secure Verifier-Based PAKE Protocols for the Industrial Internet of Things IACR ePrint · Oct 29, 2026This paper analyzes VTBSAE, a recently proposed verifier-based password-authenticated key exchange protocol, and shows it fails to resist client impersonation after server compromise. The authors propose E-VTBSAEv1, which binds the client-generated point to fresh server-side randomness while keeping the lightweight design. A formal security proof in the random-oracle model under the CDH assumption is provided. Experiments on Raspberry Pi devices show communication, storage, and runtime costs comparable to VTBSAE.

entry.title: Improving code rate and query complexity for the Ligero IOP system
entry.summary: Improving Code Rate and Query Complexity for the Ligero-IOP System IACR ePrint · Oct 29, 2026This paper analyzes and improves Ligero-style zero-knowledge proof systems. It shows that, without changing the protocol, mutual correlated agreement in the list-decoding regime yields better soundness guarantees and lower query complexity. It also proposes a Ligero variant with out-of-domain sampling that further improves soundness and allows Reed–Solomon code rates above 1/2, while keeping the constant-round structure and achieving perfect honest-verifier zero knowledge.

entry.title: A quantitative benchmark for evaluating constant-time analysis tools
entry.summary: A Quantitative Evaluation of Constant-Time Analysis Tools IACR ePrint · Oct 29, 2026This paper presents AutoBench-CT, a modular benchmark covering 64 cryptographic tasks with manually verified ground truths for each constant-time violation. The authors define the first unified quantitative metrics for operational performance, detection quality, and usability, and apply them to seven analysis tools. The paper also proposes a composite pipeline intended to strengthen constant-time security guarantees in practice.

entry.title: Measuring Duplicates and Leakage in Malware-as-Image Benchmarks
entry.summary: Measuring Duplication, Leakage, and Rendering Dependence in Malware-as-Image Benchmarks arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper audits ten benchmarks that classify malware binaries rendered as images, finding that hash-based deduplication fails to prevent leakage because distinct binaries can produce identical images. Deduplicating on image content lowers accuracy and macro-F1 on benchmarks found to be leaky. The authors also report that changing the byte-wrapping width during rendering reduces accuracy substantially, and they recommend reporting content-level duplication and a non-image baseline.

entry.title: Power-adjusting attacks on mining pools under block-dependent payout schemes
entry.summary: Power Adjusting Games Under Block-Dependent Pool Payout Schemes arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper analyzes the T-PAW power-adjusting block withholding attack under three payout schemes used in practice: PPLNS, round-based PROP, and exponential-decay EXP. It also introduces Power Adjusting Hopping (PAH), in which an attacker adjusts its power toward the pool according to round blockwork age without withholding blocks. The authors derive revenue ratios analytically and verify them with Monte Carlo simulations. They find that PROP is highly vulnerable to PAH, while PPLNS is the least vulnerable scheme. ★★★★ Notable: The authors analyze power adjusting attacks under block-dependent payout schemes, propose PAH, derive revenue ratios analytically, and report Monte Carlo verification.

entry.title: From "if" to "Oops": Turning a Branch into a Key-Recovery Oracle
entry.summary: From if to Oops: Turning a conditional into a key-recovery oracle arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies fault attacks on deterministic variants of CSIDH, including Houben's deterministic CSIDH and OSIDH-LD. Because every secret-dependent step occurs at a fixed, public point in each execution, an attacker can repeatedly fault the same step. By forcing a selection mask to zero, the attacker learns whether a secret exponent reaches a chosen threshold, and a binary search over thresholds recovers the full key with one fault per execution. The authors also argue that resisting such faults requires abandoning determinism and propose randomization-based countermeasures. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors show that fixed public points in deterministic CSIDH let repeated faults turn a branch into a key-recovery oracle. They report simulated full OSIDH-LD key recovery and ChipWhisperer measur

entry.title: Provably secure watermarking for diffusion models against removal attacks with batched detector access
entry.summary: Provably Secure Diffusion Watermarking Against Removal Adversaries with Batched Detector Access arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies latent-based watermarking for AI-generated images. The authors show that existing defenses hiding detection boundaries with secret long-term transformations fail when an adversary has batched access to a public detector, as the adversary can reconstruct the transformations. They propose a hybrid scheme combining long-term and one-time secret transformations to prevent structure reuse across samples. The paper proves the scheme is provably secure against such removal adversaries, with a tight √2 factor in perturbation budget relative to isotropic white-noise attacks. Experiments on Stable Diffusion 2.1 and XL demonstrate the attack on the existing defense and show the new scheme preserves generation quality and resists common perturbations and targeted removal attacks. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a hybrid secret-transformation diffusion watermark, prove security against batched-detector removal adversaries with a tight √2 factor, and evaluate on Stable Diffusion 2.1 and XL.

entry.title: Appreciation Teaches Unauthorized Execution: Self-Evolution Weakens Personal Agents' Defense Against Hidden Injected Instructions
entry.summary: Appreciation Teaches Unauthorized Execution: Self-Evolution Degrades the Robustness of Personal Agents to Indirect Prompt Injection arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies whether personal agents that learn from user feedback become more vulnerable to indirect prompt injection, where third parties hide instructions in external content. The authors use a two-phase setup: an adaptation phase where the user asks the agent to complete tasks from external content, then a test phase where a similar injected task is unauthorized. Across multiple domains, self-evolution raised attack success rates by 14.0 to 48.8 points under skill evolution and 3.0 to 39.3 points under reinforcement learning, compared with a non-evolving base agent. ★★★★ Notable: The authors study how self-evolving personal agents lose robustness to indirect prompt injection, reporting large attack success rate increases across skill and RL evolution.

entry.title: FlipJev: Fast black-box red teaming that finds universal adversarial suffixes for typed decision models
entry.summary: FlipJev: Fast Black-Box Red Teaming Finds Universal Adversarial Suffixes for Typed Decision Models arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies the robustness of typed decision models, language models that output decisions rather than free text. The authors propose a fast black-box query attack that does not use an attacker language model, and test it on 12 datasets. Common prompt injections fail to change correct answers, but the attack finds short suffixes that flip confident answers within minutes. These suffixes are universal and can transfer across tasks. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors report a fast black-box attack finding universal suffixes, flipping 43% of unseen documents and 90-100% of cross-task samples across 12 datasets.

entry.title: Where You Inject Matters: The Trust Region Effect in LLM Agents
entry.summary: Where You Inject Matters: The Trust Region Effect in LLM Agents arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper examines whether the location of malicious instructions in an agent's environment affects its vulnerability to indirect prompt injection. The authors built three agentic testbeds covering tool use, coding, and daily workflows, holding injection content fixed while varying placement. They find that a GPT-5.4 agent followed an unsafe instruction in a repository README or TODO file 2.6 times more often on average than the same instruction in a code or data file. They term this the trust region effect and develop learning-based attackers that select both injection placement and content. ★★★★ Notable: The authors systematically study injection placement, proposing a trust region effect and learning-based attackers; the abstract reports READMEs are followed 2.6 times more often than code or data fil

entry.title: Improved LCL Equivalences and Curve Decoding Alphabet Sizes
entry.summary: Improved LCL Equivalences and Curve Decoding Alphabet Sizes arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper refines equivalence results for Local Coordinate-wise Linear (LCL) properties, showing that all known subspace design codes, including folded Reed–Solomon codes, share the same LCL rate threshold as random linear and random Reed–Solomon codes. It applies these results to curve decoding, a property relevant to proximity gaps, correlated agreement, and mutual correlated agreement. The authors exponentially reduce the required alphabet sizes while matching the best known parameters. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend LCL equivalence to all known subspace design constructions and exponentially improve curve decoding alphabet bounds.

entry.title: Complexity of differentially private selection in federated settings
entry.summary: Complexity of Differentially Private Selection via Federated APIs arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper studies the accuracy gap of differentially private selection in federated or distributed settings. It shows that any private selection algorithm relying on the standard noisy aggregation primitive requires Ω(√d/ε) samples. To overcome this, the authors propose a new primitive implementing a version of the Sparse Vector Technique and develop an ε-differentially private selection algorithm with additive error O(log(dn)/ε). This matches the central model when n is polynomially bounded in d, and yields an exponential separation from shuffle and aggregation-based models. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a new SVT primitive, prove an Ω(√d/ε) sample lower bound for aggregation models, and match central-model selection error, yielding an exponential separation.

entry.title: How deterministic SAST and AI security agents split vulnerability detection work, measured on Snyk VulnBench 2.0
entry.summary: How Deterministic SAST and AI Security Agents Divide the Work: Coverage, Harness Policy and Cost in Snyk VulnBench 2.0 arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper evaluates deterministic static analysis (SAST) against AI coding agents and security harnesses on VulnBench 2.0, a benchmark of 108 attacker-reachable vulnerabilities across 20 open-source web applications. Snyk Code reached 82.4% recall and Claude Code with Opus 5 reached 79.3%, while combining the two engines found 101 of 108. The authors report that AI configurations also flagged at least seven real vulnerabilities absent from the reference set, and that what an AI engine misses depends on its harness as well as its model. ★★★★ Notable: The authors compare deterministic SAST with AI security agents on 108 curated vulnerabilities across 20 open-source web apps, reporting coverage and harness effects.

entry.title: Calibrating Difficulty Over Time for Diffusion Model Membership Inference
entry.summary: Difficulty Calibration Across Time for Membership Inference in Diffusion Models arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies membership inference attacks, which test whether an image was used to train a diffusion model. It argues that raw reconstruction loss is unreliable because some images are inherently easier to reconstruct, and proposes calibrating for this difficulty. Reference-Model Calibration compares a fine-tuned model against an earlier checkpoint, while Temporal Self-Calibration uses losses at neighboring diffusion timesteps from a single model. The authors report that both methods outperform prior attacks and generalize across x-, v-, and ε-prediction models.

entry.title: TextSeal2: Distortion-Free LLM Watermarking with Copula Mixing
entry.summary: TextSeal2: Distortion-Free LLM Watermarking with Copula Mixing and Memoryless Races arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper presents TextSeal2, a distortion-free watermark for large language models that keeps its signal under speculative decoding without changing the acceptance rate. It preserves output diversity and adds no measurable inference latency. The method merges multiple keys into one virtual key coupled to fresh noise via a Gaussian copula. Evaluations on three LLMs report higher detection rates than its predecessor TextSeal at equal output diversity.

entry.title: Privacy and security risks when optimizing large language models for edge devices
entry.summary: The Privacy and Security Risks of Edge LLM Optimization arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper examines optimization techniques used to deploy large language models on edge devices, aimed at reducing memory, computation, and energy costs. The authors argue that preserving task performance does not necessarily preserve security. They contend that optimization transforms information in ways that can alter representations, decision pathways, and trust boundaries, creating security drift and new attack surfaces introduced by the optimization itself.

entry.title: Efficient oversight of AI computations through rewinding
entry.summary: Efficient Scalable Oversight via Rewinding arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies how a weak verifier can check computations performed by more powerful AI systems. It introduces rewindable interactive proofs (RIPs), in which the verifier can rewind the prover to an earlier state and continue from there. The authors build a relativizing RIP for computations whose outputs are robust to changes in a small fraction of oracle answers, using no cryptography. The construction is more efficient than prior methods that do not assume a truthful prover, and a preliminary MNIST experiment is reported.

entry.title: RecHash: Segmented Hash-Entangled Chains for Stateful Sequential Authentication
entry.summary: RecHash: Segmented Hash-Entangled Chains for Stateful Sequential Authentication arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents RecHash, a stateful sequential authentication scheme built on paired hash-chain openings and an authenticated record history. It extends the 2019 hash-entangled construction by assigning each record to a predetermined chain segment, so every digest block fits its scheduled slot. The paper gives a segmented state transition, a worked example, allocation and resource results, and a renewal-free security composition theorem under authenticated history and an adaptive one-step guarantee.

entry.title: Deep learning models for continuous typing-based identity checks
entry.summary: Deep Learning Based Behavioral Drift Modeling for Continuous Biometric Authentication arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper proposes a two-level keystroke dynamics authentication system. The first level uses Temporal Convolutional Networks with contrastive learning and population-based training to verify fixed-text passwords, reaching a 3.77% equal error rate. After login, the second level monitors typing during free-text sessions with a four-model deep learning ensemble. If suspicious behavioral drift is detected, the user is sent back to the first level for re-authentication. The free-text component reports a 10.05% equal error rate.

entry.title: Understanding and Mitigating Role Spoofing in LLMs
entry.summary: Understanding and Mitigating Role Spoofing in LLMs arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies how large language models track who said what in a conversation, using both content cues such as style and structural cues such as control tokens. It shows that models are highly vulnerable to role spoofing attacks that combine fake structure and content. In a toy setting, adversarial training against content-based injections mitigates those attacks but leaves models susceptible to structure-based ones. The authors also propose a detection method using linear probes trained to predict conversational roles, which they report is effective across different settings.

entry.title: DYNAS: A Dynamic Network Penetration Testing Framework Using Deep Hierarchical RL
entry.summary: DYNAS: A Dynamic Network Penetration Testing Framework Using Deep Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper presents DYNAS, a dynamic network attack simulator that generates large parameterized scenarios with intrusion detection responses, scan false positives and negatives, temporary service outages, and action timeouts. It also introduces Pen-DHRL, a recurrent manager-worker policy that selects persistent subgoals using IDS-conditioned global context. Compared with GNN, Invariant, and Attention baselines, Pen-DHRL achieves higher reward or more captured hosts in several scenarios, and with all defensive dynamics active from training onward, it attains positive mean returns in all four scenarios.

entry.title: Training-free multi-bit image watermarking that resists attacks via latent sign clamping
entry.summary: Attack-Resilient Multi-Bit Image Watermarking Framework via Latent Coordinate Sign Clamping arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper presents a training-free watermarking method that uses the overcompleteness of diffusion latent spaces to embed multi-bit messages into arbitrary images while preserving visual quality. It adds a three-layer decoding pipeline, a steganalysis-resistant noise camouflage layer, and a dual-layer forgery defense combining perceptual hashing with CLIP-based fuzzy commitment. The authors report a 94.6% decode rate against CtrlRegen+ regeneration attacks and 98.8% forgery detection accuracy.

entry.title: ExploreRepair: Evidence-Specialized Agents for Repairing Software Vulnerabilities With Incomplete Information
entry.summary: ExploreRepair: Evidence-Specialized Agents for Vulnerability Repair under Information Constraints arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper presents ExploreRepair, a framework for automatically repairing software vulnerabilities when developers lack complete vulnerability details. Three exploration agents each examine a different aspect of the vulnerability, and aggregators combine their observations and repair proposals into a final fix. On the PatchEval and VulnLoc+ benchmarks, it reports higher repair success rates than the compared methods EvoRepair and LoopRepair without PoV tests.

entry.title: A new post-quantum encryption scheme using syndrome trellis decoding
entry.summary: Syndrome Trellis Decryption in Post-Quantum Cryptography arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper proposes a post-quantum public-key cryptosystem based on masked high-memory convolutional codes within the Niederreiter framework. The public key is built from a high-memory polynomial parity-check matrix, hidden by dense random masking and invertible linear transformations. The authors claim security margins well above classical McEliece- and Niederreiter-based systems, along with support for arbitrary message lengths and linear-time decryption.

entry.title: Perception, comprehension and projection for cyber alert validation
entry.summary: Integrating Perception, Comprehension, and Projection for Alert Validation: A Unified Cyber Situational Awareness Framework arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper examines how well three levels of cyber situational awareness (perception, comprehension, and projection) help security analysts validate alerts. The authors generate multi-level CSA with Captain and Kairos and frame alert validation as a positive-unlabelled multi-instance learning task. Experiments on the DARPA TC dataset show that comprehension-level CSA, which adds causal attack context, substantially improves validation, while richer CSA does not always help.

entry.title: Learning From Surprise Alone Absorbs Lies: Evidence-Gated Continual Learning for LLMs
entry.summary: Surprise Alone Learns Lies: Evidence-Gated Continual Learning for LLMs from Streaming Claims arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies continual learning for large language models that selects training inputs by surprise, and shows that planted falsehoods about known facts are highly surprising and get absorbed. The authors test LoRA-adapted models on streams of true and false claims using a judge verifier, regression tests, the original model's prior knowledge, and routing to trusted evidence. They find that each acceptance signal answers a different question and that none alone decides whether a claim is true.

entry.title: InferD: A Honeypot Framework for AI Inference Infrastructure
entry.summary: InferD: A Honeypot Framework for AI Inference Infrastructure arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper presents InferD, a low-interaction honeypot framework that emulates AI inference infrastructure such as LLM serving stacks, inference APIs, vector databases, and agent gateways exposed on the public internet. Its core principle, deception without inference, answers every observable request from static response pools and never executes anything an adversary submits. The framework splits emulation into four deception planes (transport, service protocol, vulnerability surface, and agentic session) and adds a provenance plane that links planted credentials to evidence of downstream model-mediated processing.

entry.title: SEAL: Sealed-query sanitization of tool outputs against indirect prompt injection
entry.summary: SEAL: Sealed Queries for Local Sanitization against Indirect Prompt Injection arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper presents SEAL, a defense against indirect prompt injection, where attacks hidden in untrusted tool outputs manipulate local LLM agents. SEAL learns a soft prompt and scoring readout offline, using a frozen task model to sanitize tool outputs by localized deletion while preserving useful evidence. On AgentDojo, attack success drops from 34.6% to 0.1%, and joint task completion rises from 51.4% to 77.5%, using about 127 times fewer defense tokens than PISanitizer. Replication on a second backbone supports applicability across model families.

entry.title: Investigating Data Flows from Android Games
entry.summary: Investigating Data Flows from Android Games arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper examines what data popular free-to-play Android puzzle games collect and where they send it. The authors analyzed over 16 GB of network traffic from 50 games. They also tested user-side countermeasures, finding that ad-blocking DNS services reduce data flows, while withholding consent or opting out can produce inconsistent behavior, including increased outgoing traffic. The measurements are released as an open dataset.

entry.title: Hardware-Aware Model Inversion in Memristive Spiking Neural Networks
entry.summary: Hardware-Aware Model Inversion in Memristive Spiking Neural Networks arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper examines whether privacy leakage from model inversion remains consistent when a spiking neural network is mapped onto memristive hardware with variability and faults. The authors propose SDMI, which combines Expectation over Transformation with surrogate gradients to optimize inputs. Leakage does not track accuracy or hardware variability monotonically; neuron-threshold perturbations raise SSIM reconstruction fidelity by up to 51.8%, while weight noise reduces leakage.

entry.title: PairWatch: A Pair-Aware Transformer for Spotting Adversarial Rendezvous in Public Satellite Catalogs
entry.summary: PairWatch: Pair-Aware Anomaly Transformer for Detecting Adversarial Rendezvous in Public Satellite Catalogs arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper proposes PairWatch, a model that detects adversarial rendezvous and proximity operations in public TLE satellite catalogs by treating satellite pairs as the unit of analysis. Its attention prior includes a sign-symmetric geometric similarity computed over relative-motion features. The authors release an open benchmark of 359 windows covering 11 documented RPO events, 100 synthetic adversarial windows, and five classes of hard negatives. PairWatch is reported as the only model that separates real RPO from operational negatives under a single threshold.

entry.title: Cybersecurity Practices of Croatian Industrial Control System Integrators
entry.summary: Cybersecurity Practices in Industrial Automation and Control Systems: a Study of Croatian System Integrators arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This study uses three focus groups with Croatian system integrators to examine how they view cybersecurity requirements, implementation challenges, and current practices in industrial automation and control systems. The integrators work with clients in energy, chemical and pharmaceutical, and food and beverage sectors. Participants reported limited cybersecurity awareness among system owners and differences in practice between smaller and larger, and domestic and foreign, firms. Their expectations about the impact of EU NIS2 regulatory pressure were divided.

entry.title: RV2GC: A paper on reconstructing the garbling boundary in a RISC-V garbled processor
entry.summary: RV2GC: Reconstructing the Garbling Boundary in a RISC-V Garbled Processor arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper presents RV2GC, a method for programmable garbled-circuit execution built around a fixed library of RISC-V instruction circuits. Public scheduling and operand routing sit outside the circuit topologies, while persistent label-encoded state links independently invoked instruction circuits. A Conditional-execution Stack and protected commits support secret-dependent branches, bounded loops, and secret-indexed memory access. Across nine benchmarks, runtime ratios relative to ARM2GC are reported.

entry.title: Judging Before Propagation: Task-Graph Contextual Integrity for Multi-Agent Privacy
entry.summary: Judging Before Propagation: Task-Graph Contextual Integrity for Multi-Agent Privacy arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper examines privacy risks in multi-agent LLM systems, where information disclosed at one step can become inappropriate once it propagates downstream through a workflow. It introduces Task-Graph Contextual Integrity (TG-CI), which models workflows as task graphs and judges disclosures by their intended propagation scope and recipients' evolving disclosure states. The authors propose two complementary enforcement policies and MAPLE-Bench, a 144-case benchmark. In the primary configuration, TG-CI reduces unauthorized disclosures by 85.8–94.1% compared with a Local-History baseline while retaining 93.6–96.1% of its task accuracy.

entry.title: Testing how seven LLMs withstand adversarial jailbreak attacks and defenses
entry.summary: Systematic Evaluation of Adversarial Jailbreaking Attacks and Defenses Across Seven Large Language Models arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper systematically tests five families of adversarial jailbreaking attacks against seven large language models and evaluates four defense mechanisms. Obfuscation attacks proved the most transferable, with a mean attack success rate of 54.3%. Self-reminder prompting was the most consistent defense, cutting attack success on Mistral-7B and Llama-3.1-8B to 10% and 5% with no false positives and no additional inference cost.

entry.title: Checking whether static analysis wrongly rules out Python code paths by comparing against execution
entry.summary: When Static Reachability Says No: Checking Joern-Based Negative Verdicts for Python Against Execution arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper presents SourceLens, a pipeline that maps Semgrep findings onto a Python program's call graph, with edges taken from Joern's code property graph. The authors ran two command-line programs under coverage and compared the recorded calls against the negative reachability verdicts. Many functions marked unreachable were in fact executed, and the missing calls often pass through values or lack call expressions. The paper also evaluates a rule that converts negative verdicts to unknown and discusses its limits.

entry.title: Does Federated Training Hurt Explanation Quality? Grad-CAM Faithfulness in Centralized vs. Federated Deepfake Detection
entry.summary: Does Federated Training Degrade Explainability? A Comparative Analysis of Grad-CAM Faithfulness in Centralized vs. Federated Deepfake Detection arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper examines whether federated learning, which shares only model updates instead of raw data, affects the quality of Grad-CAM explanations for deepfake detectors. The authors evaluate an EfficientNet-B4 detector on FaceForensics++ across five federated clients under varying degrees of data heterogeneity. They find a non-monotonic relationship: at near-IID and moderate heterogeneity, federated models match or exceed the centralized baseline, while at extreme heterogeneity the explanations become spatially incoherent and, on average, causally misleading.

entry.title: ARBITRA: A method for robust document-level ATT&CK extraction from threat reports using multiple AI experts
entry.summary: ARBITRA: Robust Document-Level ATT&CK Extraction via Multi-Expert Argumentation arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper presents ARBITRA, a system that converts cyber threat intelligence reports into structured MITRE ATT&CK mappings. Multiple role-specialized large language model experts propose candidate entities from the full report, and each candidate is verified through a quantitative bipolar argumentation framework grounded in document evidence. On ATT&CK extraction benchmarks, ARBITRA achieves higher precision than sentence-level pipelines, recent LLM systems, and frontier models including GPT-5.5, and under adversarial perturbations its precision drops about half as much as frontier-model baselines.

entry.title: DualGuard: A unified framework for memory safety during both normal and speculative program execution
entry.summary: DualGuard: Comprehensive and Efficient Memory Safety across Sequential and Speculative Execution arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper presents DualGuard, a framework that protects memory safety during both non-speculative and speculative execution. It classifies memory behaviors into four categories and identifies the minimal set of protections needed to achieve dual memory safety, avoiding redundant defenses. The framework is implemented in LLVM using a combination of static analysis and runtime enforcement. The evaluation reports that DualGuard reduces overhead by 3% to 72% compared with naive combinations of existing defenses.

entry.title: AgentHeal: Testing whether web agents can recover resources and keep their goals when access is blocked
entry.summary: AgentHeal: Evaluating Goal-Preserving Resource Recovery of Web Agents under Access Barriers arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper introduces AgentHeal, a benchmark that tests whether web agents can detect non-transient access barriers such as dead links, authentication walls, rate limits, and anti-scraping defenses. It measures whether agents can switch to legitimate alternative sources and still complete the user's exact original objective. Across nine barrier families, average task success for leading LLM backbones falls from 89.4% to 43.7% under access barriers. The authors also report that agents are often misled by look-alike sources, fail to escalate to users, violate access policies, and waste effort on futile retries.

entry.title: CLaW: Codec-Guided Adaptive Latent Watermarking for Traceable Diffusion Image Generation
entry.summary: CLaW: Codec-Guided Adaptive Latent Watermarking for Traceable Diffusion Image Generation arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper proposes CLaW, a watermarking framework that lets images from text-to-image diffusion models be traced back to individual users. A pretrained watermark codec maps each message to a latent residual, which is injected during a late denoising window. Decoding confidence feedback adaptively adjusts watermark strength. The authors report high visual fidelity and state-of-the-art robustness under image transformations.

entry.title: REALM: Identifying Minimal Task Assets for LLM Agents
entry.summary: REALM: Identifying Minimal Task Assets for LLM Agents arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper presents REALM, an approach that identifies the files, accounts, and services an LLM agent needs for a task and the uses permitted for them, applying least privilege. It separates discovering an asset from authorizing its use. Evaluated on AgentDyn with qwen3.5-flash, it reduces attack success rate from 16.6% to 0.2% across injected cases.

entry.title: Unlocking with the Heart: Users' Views on ECG-Based Biometric Login
entry.summary: Unlocking with the Heart: Investigating User Perceptions of ECG-Based Biometric Authentication arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies heart-signal (ECG) biometric authentication as a passwordless alternative to passwords. The researchers surveyed 337 adults about their authentication habits and attitudes toward security, convenience, and adoption. A separate group of 49 participants tried a simulated ECG login and a password login in a healthcare app prototype, then completed a usability questionnaire.

entry.title: PCM: A Proof-Carrying Message Protocol for Verifiable Multi-Agent Communication
entry.summary: PCM: A Proof-Carrying Message Protocol for Verifiable Multi-Agent Communication arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper proposes Proof-Carrying Messages (PCM), a protocol in which each claim an AI agent sends carries evidence, such as records from an append-only Merkle log with inclusion proofs, signed by a signer the agent cannot control. Receivers verify messages offline and label each claim as proven, unproven, or failed. On a pre-specified benchmark of 926 messages containing 712 lies, PCM accepted 10 of them (1.4%), while plain A2A accepted all 712.

entry.title: Study on whether overlaying strings helps humans compare them accurately
entry.summary: Usable String Matching by Humans through Overlaid Presentation arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper examines how well people can tell whether two character strings are identical, a task that is error-prone in settings such as bank wire transfers. Two online experiments with 178 participants varied string length, the type of difference, alignment, and whether strings were shown adjacent or overlaid. Overlaid presentation was substantially faster and more accurate for long strings, but mean error rates remained at least 4 percent.

entry.title: DeepDiff: A Method for Checking Whether Security Patches Cause Regressions
entry.summary: DeepDiff: Neuro-Dynamic Regression-Freedom Checking for Security Patch Validation arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper presents DeepDiff, a technique that checks whether AI-generated security patches introduce regressions. It compares candidate patches against the original vulnerable program using non-crashing inputs, to see whether a patch removes the vulnerability-triggering crash while preserving other intended behavior. The authors also introduce a dataset of correct and incorrect patch candidates for open-source memory-safety vulnerabilities from CyberGym, and compare test input generation methods, a purely neural checker, and a hybrid of dynamic analysis and neural techniques. Experiments show the approach is effective for validating security patches, while the authors outline remaining challenges.

entry.title: Defense-aware explainable AI for finding vulnerable input features in optimal power flow analysis
entry.summary: A Defense-Aware Explainable AI Framework for Feature-Level Vulnerability Analysis in Optimal Power Flow arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper addresses the growing cyber risk to power system operation as machine-learning surrogate models for optimal power flow (OPF) come into wider use. It proposes a defense-aware explainable AI framework that combines an OPF surrogate model, which captures input-to-output dependencies, with a vanilla autoencoder, which captures input-to-input dependencies. Shapley-based explanations from both models are used to build a feature-level vulnerability metric. Experiments on IEEE test systems show it identifies security-relevant vulnerabilities more accurately than approaches using only the OPF surrogate model.

entry.title: IDSForge: A Network Intrusion Detector That Explains Itself with Learned Rules
entry.summary: IDSForge: Self-Explaining Network Intrusion Detection Through Neural Behavioral Rule Learning arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper presents IDSForge, an anomaly-based network intrusion detection system that learns explicit, executable behavioral rules from benign traffic, so its detection logic is interpretable by design. The same rule set is used for both detection and explanation and can be run directly by NIDS engines such as Suricata. The authors report that IDSForge reduces F1 error by 5.7 to 47 times relative to state-of-the-art anomaly-based baselines and sustains 7.8 Gbps throughput when deployed in Suricata.

entry.title: CARI: A runtime feedback attack on coding agents across developer boundaries
entry.summary: CARI: Cross-Boundary Adversarial Runtime Injection in Coding-Agent Workflows arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper introduces CARI (Cross-Boundary Adversarial Runtime Injection), an attack in which a malicious peer-controlled development component, such as a backend service or CI job, embeds hidden instructions in its runtime feedback. A victim's coding agent treats this feedback as normal debugging guidance and may perform unauthorized actions. The authors build ten CARI attacks covering resource exhaustion, information exposure, and development-state manipulation. Across four languages and five models the attacks succeed in 94.8% of trials, and they transfer to Codex (61.3%) and Claude Code (58.7%).

entry.title: Trustworthy distributed machine learning across cloud, edge and IoT, with a survey of security, privacy and robustness under heterogeneity
entry.summary: Trustworthy Distributed Machine Learning in Cloud-Edge-IoT Systems: A Heterogeneity-Aware Survey of Security, Privacy, and Robustness arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This survey examines security in distributed machine learning, including federated learning, which it treats as a high-risk case. It defines the assets, adversaries, and trust assumptions involved and analyzes how data, system, and trust heterogeneity affect convergence, fairness, and defense reliability. The paper compares layered defenses such as robust aggregation, differential privacy, secure aggregation, and trusted execution environments. It closes with guidance on deployment, evaluation, and governance.

entry.title: Adversarial process disturbances at a fixed false-alarm budget: evaluating anomaly detectors on a simulator and a real plant
entry.summary: Adversarial Process Disturbances at a Deployable Alarm Budget: Detector Evaluation on a Simulator and a Real Plant arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper evaluates eleven anomaly detectors on a simulated chemical process and a sodium thermal-hydraulic facility, perturbing only temperature, pressure, flow and valve. Measured at a declared false-alarm budget, detection collapses on real plant telemetry while the simulator results appeared deployable. Sequential valve manipulation evades nearly the whole detector panel.

entry.title: Improving image forensics using partial C2PA provenance data
entry.summary: Enhanced image forensics through partial C2PA-based provenance information arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies forensic analysis of images carrying partial C2PA Content Credentials, which record only the last operations applied while earlier provenance must be investigated through signal forensics. The authors propose a two-step strategy: reconstructing the operations applied by the last signer through structural analysis of the partial credentials, then using that reconstruction to adapt a forensic detector. In a case study on synthetic image detection, the strategy significantly improved state-of-the-art detectors on test images postprocessed with C2PA-enabled software.

entry.title: A comparative study of post-quantum cryptography for automotive communication
entry.summary: The use of post-quantum cryptography in the automotive context arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper compares post-quantum cryptography schemes for automotive communication, considering threats from quantum algorithms such as Shor's and Grover's. Simulations on two hardware platforms, using OMNeT++, Veins, INET and SUMO, test ML-KEM (Kyber), ML-DSA (Dilithium) and FALCON. Kyber shows low key encapsulation latency, Dilithium gives balanced signature performance, and FALCON has high key-generation and signing costs but efficient verification.

entry.title: STAR: A Scalable TEE-Based System for Anonymous Rate Limiting
entry.summary: STAR: Scalable TEE-based Anonymous Rate-limiter arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper presents STAR, a system that uses server-side trusted execution environments (TEEs) to enable anonymous rate limiting, protecting internet services from attacks such as TLS/HTTP floods while preserving user privacy. The authors address the risk that malicious services could infer user secrets through memory-access patterns by adding countermeasures against secret-dependent memory accesses, which they assess with dynamic analysis. They also design a secure sharding mechanism to distribute client requests across servers. The paper reports that STAR processes authentication requests in tens of microseconds and handles about 13.9K requests per second per CPU core.

entry.title: Session-Bound Behavioral Watermarking for Autonomous LLM Agents
entry.summary: Session-Bound Behavioral Watermarking for Autonomous LLM Agents arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper addresses how to embed ownership evidence in the action trajectories produced by LLM agents operating through Web interfaces and tools, so that a disputed log can be attributed to its agent owner. It notes that existing behavioral watermarking work focuses on detection, removal, rewriting, or imitation, and does not directly test whether repeated observation of watermarked trajectories enables cross-session forgery. The authors propose AgentAnchor, a session-keyed behavioral watermark, together with a trusted verifier that checks disputed logs without rerunning the agent.

entry.title: A black-box attack that sends fake traffic reports to disrupt AI-controlled traffic lights
entry.summary: A Minimally Informed Black-Box Fake-Report Attack on DRL Traffic-Signal Control arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies how deep reinforcement learning traffic-signal controllers that rely on vehicle-to-infrastructure reports can be attacked with false data. The attacker has no access to the model and sees only traffic on her own approach, and she trains an imitation surrogate to craft bounded fake vehicle counts. The results show these fake reports significantly increase waiting times on other approaches while barely changing her own. The paper also finds that simply reporting the maximum feasible queue is as damaging, pointing to the V2I sensing channel itself as the exposed vulnerability.

entry.title: How privacy professionals actually conduct privacy and data protection impact assessments today
entry.summary: The State of the Practice in Privacy Impact Assessments: Understanding the Professionals' Perspectives, Experiences, and Current Procedures arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper interviews 26 privacy professionals from 17 countries about how they plan and carry out Privacy Impact Assessments and Data Protection Impact Assessments. Using reflexive thematic analysis, it finds low adherence to established DPIA methodologies and a perceived neglect of data subjects' interests. The study also discusses building Fundamental Rights Impact Assessments on top of DPIAs and the potential for holistic assessments, noting concerns about assessment fatigue.

entry.title: Is It My Preference? A Role Grounding Attack That Misattributes Preferences in Agent Memory
entry.summary: Is it my preference? Role Grounding Attack against Agent's Memory via Social Interaction arXiv · Oct 28, 2026LLM-based agents share experiences on social platforms and remember new preferences, but existing memory systems can misattribute roles to principals. The paper formalizes the Role Grounding Attack (RGA), which uses nested conversations so that a victim agent records an attacker's preference as the victim user's preference. The authors instantiate RGA as tool selection manipulation and privacy leakage, and evaluate it across five memory systems and six language models. Both attack types achieve high success rates, which the authors argue calls for stronger role grounding. ★★★★ Notable: The authors formalize Role Grounding Attack, exploiting role misattribution in agent memory, and report evaluations across five memory systems and six models for tool manipulation and privacy leakage.

entry.title: SPARSEBLEED: A Hardware Attack Bypassing Privacy Defenses via Sparsity Optimizations
entry.summary: SPARSEBLEED: Bypassing Attribute-Inference Defenses via Sparsity Optimizations arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper presents SparseBleed, a hardware-level attack that infers sensitive input attributes from a single query by exploiting timing signatures of sparsity-driven execution paths in accelerators. It works across Intel AVX2/AVX-512/AMX, NVIDIA Ampere Tensor Cores, and several sparse and dense libraries. The authors evaluate the attack on Texas-100X and compare mitigations, finding that disabling sparsity optimizations is costly while a padding defense adds about 7.24% average overhead. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a hardware-level attribute-stealing attack exploiting sparsity timing, reporting 66.39% Sex inference on Texas-100X and evaluating a padding defense's overhead.

entry.title: How Open-Source Software Adopts Post-Quantum Cryptography: Practices and Challenges
entry.summary: Understanding Post-Quantum Cryptography Adoption: Practices, Challenges, and Evolution in Open-Source Software arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper mines 114,361 commits and 5,713 issues across 179 open-source repositories to study how projects implement and maintain post-quantum cryptography (PQC) support. About 90% of PQC-related commits concern maintenance of existing support, and build, packaging, dependency, and functional failures account for roughly half of the categorized issues. After the 2024 NIST standards were finalized, standardized algorithm names appeared in more than 80% of analyzed PQC changes, but first implementations did not significantly increase. ★★★★ Notable: The authors mine 114,361 commits and 5,713 issues across 179 repositories, building an 11-category taxonomy of PQC challenges and releasing the dataset and pipeline.

entry.title: Encore: Turning Public Exploit PoCs into Threat Hunting Rules
entry.summary: Set an Exploit to Catch an Exploit: Compiling Public Proofs of Concept into Threat Hunting Rules arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper observes that public exploit code for new vulnerabilities usually appears before detection rules for their exploitation. The authors present Encore, which compiles a public Python proof-of-concept exploit into CVE-specific hunting rules over a web service's existing logs, without running the code. The paper reports that Encore's rules find 43 of 45 evaluated CVEs, separate exploit payloads from harmless matched requests, and raise no alerts across 27,081 legitimate and crawl requests. ★★★★ Notable: The authors compile public PoC exploits into hunting rules without execution, reporting results on 45 CVEs against Splunk's public attack data.

entry.title: Backdoors in AI agents planted through poisoned pretraining data
entry.summary: Agentic Backdoors via Pretraining Poisoning arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The authors pretrained Qwen3 models from scratch at 0.6B, 1.7B, and 4B sizes, then post-trained each into a command-line agent. They show that poisoning just 0.1% of the pretraining corpus can implant a backdoor that makes the agent execute attacker-chosen commands on a user's machine when a trigger is present, while behaving normally otherwise. Attack success rate rises with model size, reaching about 92% for the 4B model at a 0.1% poison rate, and remains positive even at 0.0005%. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors show pretraining poisoning can implant a remote code execution backdoor in agents, reporting about 92% attack success for a 4B Qwen3 model at a 0.1% poison rate.

entry.title: When Skills Tell Agents Not to Ask: A Study of Oversight-Loosening Directives in AI Agent Skills
entry.summary: When Skills Tell Agents Not to Ask: A Large-Scale Study of Oversight Directives in Agent Skills arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper studies oversight-loosening directives in agent skills, reusable instruction packages built around a SKILL.md file, such as instructions to proceed without approval or to bypass checks with --no-verify. The authors analyzed 1.53 million English skills from GitSkills, hand-labeled 2,097 units, and trained a detector to scale the analysis. About one in seventeen skills contains such a directive, and skills that run shell code, install packages, or use sudo are more likely to contain one. Existing open-source scanners catch at most 46% of these directives with low precision. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors present the first large-scale study of oversight-loosening directives, analyzing 1.53 million skills, hand-labeling 2,097 units, and training a detector to scale.

entry.title: FVH-Bench: A Benchmark for Image Generator Safety Beyond Obviously Harmful Pictures
entry.summary: FVH-Bench: Evaluating Image Generator Safety Beyond Overtly Harmful Imagery arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper defines functional visual harm (FVH) as the risk from what generated images enable, such as instructions or deceptive artifacts, rather than only what they depict. The authors introduce FVH-Bench, which contains 669 prompts covering five harmful visual functions and ten risk domains. Evaluation of 11 image generators found they rarely refuse these requests and often produce artifacts that fulfill the harmful functions. Existing safety detectors also show limited coverage of FVH. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose functional visual harm and a 669-prompt benchmark, evaluating 11 image generators and existing safety detectors beyond overtly harmful content.

entry.title: WebMaze: Diverting LLM-Powered Web Scanners with Decoy Pages
entry.summary: WebMaze: Defending Against LLM-Powered Web Scanners with Functionality-Coupled Deception arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper studies how large language model-based scanners probe web applications and proposes WebMaze, a defense that steers them away from real pages. WebMaze places traps inside genuine pages that connect to generated interactive decoy worlds built from existing views, without changing the real functionality. In experiments across 12 web applications and three LLM-based scanners, decoy pages made up an average of 93.0% of distinct pages requested per run, even when scanners were told about the decoys.

entry.title: Security risks of coding agent memory files
entry.summary: Security Impact of Coding Agent's Memory Files arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper examines whether project memory files such as CLAUDE.md, which coding agents load automatically at each session, can be used as an attack surface. The authors built two malicious memory files for each of 12 CWE classes and tested Claude Code and OpenCode on 36 SecRepoBench tasks. The change in secure completion rate ranged from -8 to +6 percentage points, and the agents differed in whether they disclosed the file's influence to developers.

entry.title: GI-RTL-Fuzz: LLM-based grammar-guided RTL test generation for differential fuzzing of simulators
entry.summary: GI-RTL-Fuzz: Grammar-Informed RTL Generation with LLMs for End-to-End Differential Simulator Fuzzing arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper introduces GI-RTL-Fuzz, a fuzzing framework that uses large language models to generate RTL test cases. It guides generation with Backus-Naur Form (BNF) grammar coverage information to reach complex, rarely tested Verilog language features. Through differential testing across RTL simulators, the framework reports previously unknown inconsistencies in the linting and simulation results of major Verilog simulators.

entry.title: Neural network decoder for error correction in QC-MDPC-based McEliece encryption codes
entry.summary: Recurrent Bipartite Graph Neural Networks for QC-MDPC Error Decoding in McEliece Cryptosystems arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper addresses decoding of QC-MDPC codes, a post-quantum cryptography component, where classical belief propagation often fails due to short graph cycles. Such failures can leak secret key information. The authors propose a Recurrent Bipartite Graph Neural Network with GRUs in its message-passing framework, trained with a multi-topology curriculum.
